meta.titolo: Electrician's quote by voice, with your own price list
meta.descrizione: You describe the site visit and get a draft electrician's quote: light points, sockets and consumer unit, with prices from your own price list. The customer accepts online.

elettricista.riga: Light points, sockets, consumer unit, dedicated lines and dichiarazione di conformità (declaration of conformity).
elettricista.h1: Electrician's quote: you tell it, and the draft comes out with your price list
elettricista.sottotitolo: Light points, sockets, consumer unit, chases and dichiarazione di conformità (declaration of conformity). When the site visit is done, you say it the way you'd tell a colleague: the draft uses only the prices from your price list and flags what's missing.

esempio.titolo: What you say, what you get
esempio.intro: A made-up partial rewire, said in one go as soon as you get back in the van. On the right you can see how the system keeps the simple light points apart from the two-way one, counts the sockets, puts the consumer unit on its own line and asks how many sockets the customer wants in the bedroom.
esempio.lavoro: Living room and bedroom, partial rewire
esempio.dettatura: Allora, appartamento del signor Colombo, terzo piano. In soggiorno rifaccio tutto: sei prese normali, due prese TV e tre punti luce, uno deviato vicino alla portafinestra. In camera due punti luce semplici e le prese ai lati del letto, quante non l'ha ancora deciso. Il quadro è vecchio, lo cambio: centralino da dodici moduli con il differenziale e tre magnetotermici. Poi una linea dedicata per il forno, saranno otto metri. Le tracce le chiude il muratore, quelle non le metto. I lampadari li ha già comprati lui, sono quattro, glieli monto io. L'antenna non la tocco, la sistema l'antennista.

voci.titolo: Typical items in an electrician's quote
voci.intro: Points, circuits, protection devices and paperwork: these are the lines that show up when you work on the wiring of a home. You set the price of each point and it comes from your price list; a point that isn't in your price list is left to be priced.

righe.nota: One light controlled by one switch. The most common point, in every room.
Controlled from two places: hallway and bed, start and end of a corridor.
From three places or more: stairs, long corridors, rooms with three doors.
Bi-pass or Schuko socket for normal use. It's a good idea to say which type of socket is included.
Oven, induction hob, washing machine, air conditioner: its own line with its own protection.
Coaxial or satellite socket. If the aerial is not included, write it down.
RJ45 socket for network or phone, with the cable run to the collection point.
State the modules (12, 24, 36): the client understands what they're paying for and you avoid arguments later.
Kept separate from the consumer unit, so the client can see the protective devices you fit.
One per circuit: lights, sockets, kitchen, washing machine.
The main line from the meter to the home's consumer unit. Counted by the metre.
If the bricklayer does the filling and making good, write that they're excluded.
The client's chandeliers and ceiling lights: fitting only, the material is theirs.
Supply and fitting. For IVA it's a bene significativo (significant good): see below.
Work charged by the hour, when you don't know in advance how long it will take.
With the required attachments. Many people include it in the price: it's up to you, but write it down.

prezzare.titolo: How to price an electrician's job
prezzare.intro: The way of pricing changes from one electrician to another, and that's fine. What matters is that the client understands what's inside each line, because that's where arguments start at the end of the job.

punti.testo: This is the most common way in homes: each light point or socket has its own price, with conduit, box, cable and mechanism. Write whether the faceplate is included and which range, because designer plates and mechanisms change the total.

For a complete rewire the client often wants a single number. You can give it, but keep the breakdown by room: if halfway through they change their mind about a bedroom, you know straight away how much the price changes.
Cutting the chases is your job, filling them and making good the plaster often isn't. If the bricklayer does it, put it under the exclusions: it's the first thing the client takes for granted.

Chandeliers, ceiling lights, faceplates bought by them: the line becomes fitting only. The system understands this when you say «he's already bought them himself» and doesn't suggest the item with supply included.
During the job the client always asks for one more socket. If the quote has the price of a single point, the change works itself out and you don't have to redo everything.
Fault finding and small jobs are done by the hour, with the call-out charged separately if you charge for it. Write when the clock starts, so the client has no surprises.

documenti.titolo: Documents, rules and IVA to keep in mind
documenti.intro: An electrician's quote that mentions the right documents shows the client they know who they're dealing with. These are the things that come up most often in jobs in homes.

punti.testo: When the work is finished, the installer firm gives the customer the dichiarazione di conformità (declaration of conformity) required by DM 37/2008, with its attachments: the design, the report on the materials used, the diagram of the system as built and a copy of the certificate of technical and professional requirements. Write in the quote whether it is included in the price.

Above certain thresholds the installation must be designed by a professional registered with the professional body. For homes, DM 37/2008 sets contracted power above 6 kW or floor area above 400 m². If it's needed, say so in the quote: it's a cost the client must know about beforehand.

The CEI 64-8 standard sets the minimum provisions for home installations, in three levels: level 1 is the minimum for a new or rewired installation. Writing the level in the quote helps the client compare different offers.

A system redone in a flat is usually maintenance work, with IVA (VAT) at 10%. But the video intercom is a bene significativo (a "significant good"): the 10% only applies to it up to the value of the rest of the work, and the part above that goes at 22%. If the item is marked in your price list as a bene significativo, the draft asks you how much the device is worth inside that line and uses that figure to split the IVA.

If you install systems in a building for a customer with a partita IVA (VAT number), the inversione contabile (reverse charge) often applies: you don't put IVA (VAT) on the invoice, the customer applies it. Today the system calculates the 10%, the 22% and the split of the beni significativi (significant goods); the inversione contabile not yet, so with these customers check the total before sending the quote.

documenti.avvertenza: These notes are there to guide you and don't replace the advice of your accountant or consultant. Rules and rates can change: always check the specific case.

straniero.titolo: If the client doesn't speak Italian
straniero.testo: The people who call an electrician are often foreigners who have just bought a home and found an old system, or offices of foreign companies adding workstations. For them the quote can go out in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch: light points and sockets with the translation underneath, the Italian text as the one that counts legally, and the withdrawal form in their language. You check the draft in Italian.

voci.d: Can I put per-point items and lump-sum items in the same quote?
voci.r: Yes. Each line has its own unit: light points and sockets by number, the main line by the metre, the dichiarazione di conformità (declaration of conformity) as a lump sum. The system uses the unit of the item in your price list and redoes the calculation if you give the measurements another way.

voci.d: I don't know yet how many sockets the customer wants in the bedroom. What happens?
voci.r: The system doesn't guess: the line is left without a quantity and you get a direct question, «how many sockets in the bedroom?». Answer when you know, and the total updates.

voci.d: Does the dichiarazione di conformità (declaration of conformity) go in the quote?
voci.r: You don't have to write it in, but it's worth it: if it's included in the price the customer sees that, and if it's separate there are no surprises. You can keep it as a fixed item in your price list, so it goes into every system quote.

voci.d: The builder makes good the chases. How do I stop the customer thinking that's down to me?
voci.r: Say it when you describe the job, «the builder makes good the chases». It ends up in the exclusions of the quote, written plainly under the items.

voci.d: The flat is over 6 kW contracted. How do I put the design in the quote?
voci.r: If the design is done by a professional paid by the customer, say so when you describe the job, as an exclusion: «system design paid for by the customer». If you get it done and pass the cost on, keep it as a lump-sum item in your price list: it goes into the draft like the other lines.

voci.d: The customer wants a different range of cover plates from the one in my price list.
voci.r: If you name the range when you describe the job and it isn't in your price list, the line is left to be priced, highlighted, and you put the price in yourself. If you get that range often, add it to your price list as its own item.

voci.d: A fault-finding job with the call-out: how do I put it in?
voci.r: With two items in your price list: the call-out as a lump sum and the fault-finding by the hour. If you don't say how many hours you expect when you describe the job, the hourly line is left without a quantity and asks you for it.

meta.titolo: Plumber's quote by voice, with your own price list
meta.descrizione: The plumber's quote for bathrooms, kitchens and drains: you describe the site visit, the draft uses only the prices in your price list and the customer accepts from the link.

idraulico.riga: Bathroom refits, water and waste points, sanitaryware, leaks and kitchen connections.
idraulico.h1: Plumber's quote: you leave the customer's bathroom and the draft is already ready
idraulico.sottotitolo: Bathroom refits, kitchen moves, drains, leaks. You describe what you saw while it's still fresh, even by dictating it on the phone: prices come only from your price list, and anything you haven't said comes back as a question.

esempio.intro: A bathroom to redo with the bath becoming a shower, plus two small jobs in the kitchen and the utility room. On the right you can see how the system counts the connections, measures the waste pipe by the metre up to the stack, keeps the sanitaryware bought by the customer as fitting only, and asks how many connections are needed in the utility room.
esempio.lavoro: Bathroom refit, small jobs in kitchen and utility room
esempio.dettatura: Dunque, casa della signora Ferrari. Il bagno si rifà tutto: smonto i sanitari vecchi e tolgo la vasca, al posto della vasca va un piatto doccia ottanta per centoventi. Rifaccio carico e scarico per lavabo, vaso, bidet e doccia, quindi quattro attacchi. Lo scarico va rifatto fino alla colonna, saranno sei metri abbondanti. Vaso e bidet sospesi, con la rubinetteria, li ha già comprati lei: io li monto e metto i telai. In cucina sposto il lavello di un metro e mezzo verso la finestra. In lavanderia vuole gli attacchi per lavatrice e forse asciugatrice, quanti non l'ha ancora deciso. Piastrelle e ripristini dei muri li fa il piastrellista, non sono miei.

voci.titolo: The items that come up in a plumber's quote
voci.intro: From the water point to the frame of the wall-hung fixture, these are the lines a bathroom or kitchen is broken down into. The price of each connection is yours and comes from your price list; a special part that isn't in your price list is left to be priced.

righe.nota: Toilet, bidet, basin: per piece. Say whether taking it to the tip is included.
A bath set into brickwork is not a freestanding bath: if you already know, write it in the name of the item.
The supply for each fitting, from the manifold or the main line to the connection.
The waste for each fitting up to the main pipe of the bathroom.

righe.voce: Tubazione di scarico fino alla colonna
righe.nota: The run that goes to the building's shared stack. Counted per metre, with special pieces and fall.
With the valves for each fitting: whoever wants it understands its value if they see it on a separate line.
With the shower waste and the connection to the drain. The shower enclosure is usually another item.

righe.voce: Telaio per sanitari sospesi con cassetta a incasso
righe.nota: The part that holds a wall-hung toilet or bidet. It has to be built into the wall or closed in: write who does it.
Fitting only, when the customer buys the sanitaryware.
Countertop basin, wall-hung or on a unit: it's best to keep the unit to be assembled separate.
Basin, bidet, shower, sink. For IVA, bathroom taps and fittings count as a «bene significativo» (significant good, which affects the reduced IVA rate).
Supply, waste and isolation valve.
Supply and waste taken to the new position. If the move is long, better priced per metre.
To shut off one fitting or one bathroom without shutting off the whole house.
When you don't know where the leak is until you open up. Making good is separate.
Sinks, showers, stacks: by the hour, with the equipment specified if you charge for it.
With the report on the materials used. If it's included in the price, say so.

prezzare.titolo: How to price a plumbing job
prezzare.intro: Every plumber has their own way of working things out. What saves you from an argument at the end of the job is that the customer can see what's inside each line and what's left out.

punti.titolo: Per water point and per waste point
punti.testo: In bathrooms the clearest way is to count the connections: supply and waste for each fitting. Write where the point starts from (manifold, main line, stack), because a point far from the drain doesn't cost the same as one close by.

punti.titolo: The bathroom as a lump sum, but with the detail underneath
punti.testo: The customer asks ‘how much for the bathroom?’ and wants one number. Give it to them, but keep the lines: when halfway through the job they decide to add the bidet or move the shower, you know straight away how much the bill changes.

If they buy them, the line becomes fitting only. Also write that missing pieces or ones that arrive broken are not your responsibility: with sanitaryware bought online it happens more than the customer imagines.

Breaking out to get to the pipes is often yours, closing up and redoing tiles almost never. Put it in the exclusions with the name of who does it, so the customer doesn't think making good is included.
You don't know what a leak will cost until you find it. Price it by the hour, with the call-out separate if you charge for it, and write that making good walls and floors is assessed afterwards.

The bath, sanitaryware and old pipes have to be taken away. If you only say «I'll take it all away myself», the haulage stays included in the removal. If you want a separate line, keep the item in your price list and say the quantity: «one cubic metre of rubble to take to the tip».

documenti.titolo: Documents, paperwork and IVA in plumbing jobs
documenti.intro: The things a careful customer asks you, or that it's better to say before they ask. They apply to plumbing jobs in homes.

punti.testo: Water and sanitary systems fall under the DM 37/2008 (the Italian decree on installations in buildings). When the job is finished, the installing firm gives the client the dichiarazione di conformità (declaration of conformity), with the report on the materials used and the design. For a home system the design doesn't have to be done by a professional on the register: the firm's technical manager can draw it up.

Renewing or replacing the existing water and sanitary system and the sanitaryware counts as edilizia libera (works that need no permit), according to the glossary of the DM 2 marzo 2018. Making a bathroom where there wasn't one before is instead manutenzione straordinaria (major works; DPR 380/2001, art. 3) and needs a filing with the Comune (town hall). If the filing isn't yours, write it in the exclusions.

A bathroom redone in a home is as a rule maintenance, at 10%. But sanitaryware and bathroom taps are beni significativi (significant goods) under the DM 29/12/1999: if their value is more than that of all the rest of the work, the difference goes at 22%, and on the invoice their value must be shown separately. If they are marked in your price list as beni significativi, the draft asks you how much the item is worth inside each line and uses that figure to split the IVA.

punti.titolo: If the customer buys the sanitaryware
punti.testo: According to the Agenzia delle Entrate (the Italian tax office, circolare 15/E of 2018), the 10% on beni significativi (significant goods) only applies when the person doing the work supplies them. If the customer buys them separately, they pay the shop's standard rate, and you invoice the fitting.

punti.titolo: Work for customers with a partita IVA (VAT number)
punti.testo: If you redo the plumbing of an office, a bar or a building firm doing a renovation, the inversione contabile (reverse charge) normally applies (DPR 633/1972, art. 17, comma 6): the invoice goes out without IVA (VAT) and the customer applies it. Not with a private customer. Today the system calculates the 10%, the 22% and the split of the beni significativi (significant goods); the inversione contabile not yet, so in these cases check the total before sending it.

documenti.avvertenza: This is just to point you in the right direction, not tax or technical advice: every job has its own details, and the rules change. Before applying them to a real case, get your accountant (commercialista) to confirm them.

straniero.titolo: When the customer speaks another language
straniero.testo: The owner who lives abroad and rents out the flat calls you about a leak and wants the quote before authorising the work; the foreign family who have just bought a home want to redo the bathroom. The quote can reach them in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch, with connections and sanitaryware translated item by item, the Italian text as the one that counts legally, and the withdrawal form in their language. You approve it in Italian.

voci.d: I'm redoing a whole bathroom. Is it better to give a lump-sum price or price item by item?
voci.r: You can do both: you describe the bathroom piece by piece and in the draft you get lines with quantities. If your price list has a lump-sum «rifacimento bagno» (full bathroom refit) item, you use it; otherwise keep the breakdown, which also helps when the customer changes their mind halfway through the job.

voci.d: The customer has bought the toilet, bidet and mixer taps online. What changes in the quote?
voci.r: Say so when you describe the job, for example «she bought the sanitaryware herself». The lines become fitting only, with no supply. If missing or faulty parts aren't your responsibility, write that in the name of the fitting items, so the customer reads it on the PDF.

voci.d: I say «a good six metres» of waste pipe. What ends up in the draft?
voci.r: A per-metre line with the quantity you said, in the unit of your price list item. You see the rough measurement written out, correct it if needed and only then approve.

voci.d: I've got the wholesaler's price list, not mine. Can I upload that?
voci.r: The system uses the prices you upload, and only those: if you upload purchase prices, those go in the quote. Better to upload your price list with your selling prices, even from a photo if it's on paper, and check the items before using them.

voci.d: The customer is a building firm doing a renovation. Do I have to put IVA (VAT) on it?
voci.r: Often not: between businesses with a partita IVA (VAT number), for systems in buildings, the inversione contabile (reverse charge) applies. Today the system doesn't calculate it yet, so with a business customer check the total with your accountant before sending the quote.

voci.d: The new bathroom goes where there used to be a storage room. Do I write that in the quote?
voci.r: Yes, because it counts as manutenzione straordinaria (extraordinary maintenance) and needs a filing with the Comune (town council). If the customer's technician handles it, say so when you describe the job, «the paperwork is done by their surveyor»: it ends up in the exclusions under the items.

voci.d: I'm moving the sink by a metre and a half. Do I price it as a lump sum or by the metre?
voci.r: However you have it in your price list. If the moving item is a lump sum, the line comes out as one; if it's by the metre, the measurement you gave when describing the job becomes the quantity. For long moves the per-metre item stops you giving the work away.

meta.titolo: Painter and decorator quote in a few minutes
meta.descrizione: A painter and decorator's quote from the site visit you talk through: walls, ceilings, filling and anti-mould, with prices from your own price list. The customer accepts online.

imbianchino.riga: Painting, wall preparation, anti-mould treatment, gloss paint on doors and radiators.
imbianchino.h1: Painter and decorator quote: you measure the rooms, you tell it, and the draft does the sums
imbianchino.sottotitolo: Walls, ceilings, filling, skim coats, colours and gloss paints. You walk round the flat with your tape measure, then tell it room by room: the draft only uses prices from your price list, shows the measurements in the unit of your items and asks you for whatever is missing.

esempio.titolo: Room by room, the way you'd say it out loud
esempio.intro: Three rooms to repaint, with a patch of mould, a few cracks and a ceiling that's flaking. On the right you can see how the system works the square metres out again from the room measurements, keeps the scraping on its own line, marks the small bedroom as labour only and asks how many doors to paint in gloss.
esempio.dettatura: Appunto per i Galli, appartamento di tre locali. Soggiorno quattro e mezzo per tre e ottanta, altezza normale: pareti e soffitto, due mani di idropittura bianca. In camera grande c'è la muffa nell'angolo della finestra, una fascia di un metro e mezzo più o meno: la tratto e ci do l'antimuffa. La cameretta la vogliono azzurra, la tinta l'ha già presa la signora, quindi lì solo manodopera. Nel corridoio ci sono delle crepe da stuccare, saranno una quindicina di metri di parete. Il soffitto del bagno va raschiato perché si stacca, è un due per due. Le porte interne da smaltare, quante non l'hanno ancora deciso. Copro pavimenti e mobili io. Spostare i mobili no, lo fanno loro prima che arrivi.

voci.titolo: Typical items in a painter and decorator's quote
voci.intro: Preparation, paints, enamels and protection: in painting and decorating, the quote is won or lost on how you separate these lines. The price per square metre is yours and comes from your price list; a special finish that isn't in your price list is left to be priced.

righe.nota: Dust sheets, tape, cardboard. Write whether moving the furniture is included or is up to the customer.
When the old paint is flaking or has formed a crust. It's the item the customer tends not to see.
Cracks and hairline cracks by the linear metre. For isolated holes some people prefer a lump sum.
For damaged or uneven walls. Write how many coats are included.
The sealer before the paint, on new, skimmed or powdery walls.
Two coats, walls or ceilings. State the product or range, so the comparison is like for like.
For kitchens, hallways, children's bedrooms: more hard-wearing, and the customer needs to know it's a different thing.
The difference compared with white: the colour, plus extra coats on dark or strong colours.
Kept separate from the walls, because it's more work and it's often the only thing to do.
Cleaning, treatment product and anti-mould paint on the affected area.
Per door leaf, with or without frame: write it down, because frames take time.
Per item, with preparation. If the radiator has to come off, you need a plumber.
Per linear metre, with brushing off the rust and rust-proofing if needed.
On the sharp external corners of hallways and entrances, before the skim coat.
Taking off the sheets and tape and leaving the home liveable. Saying it's included costs little and customers like it.
Touch-ups, small repairs, jobs you can't measure beforehand.

prezzare.titolo: How to price a painting job
prezzare.intro: In painting, the part that gets argued over is almost never the paint: it's the preparation, and how you counted the metres. Writing it down properly saves you the phone call from the customer with the tape measure in hand.

punti.testo: Measuring openings as solid (vuoto per pieno) or deducting doors and windows: it's up to you, but write it in the name of the item or in the notice at the bottom of the quote. A customer who redoes the sums with a different method will always find a difference, and without a written line they think you inflated it.

Scraping, filling, skimming, sealer. If you fold them into the per-metre price of the paint, your quote looks expensive next to someone who puts one coat over the dirt. Kept separate, the customer can see the difference between the two jobs.

punti.titolo: White, colour and number of colours
punti.testo: Colour costs more than white, and a room with two shades costs more than a room with one. Keep the coloured item separate in your price list, and write how many shades are included per room.
If they bring the paint, the line becomes labour only. Write that the quantity of paint is up to them: if the tin runs out halfway across a wall, the time lost isn't your fault.

punti.titolo: Mould: the treatment is not the cure
punti.testo: Anti-mould treatment fixes the wall, not the damp that causes it. Write it plainly on the quote: if the cause is a thermal bridge or a leak, the mould comes back, and the customer needs to know that beforehand.
Moving the furniture, taking the radiators off, taking the doors down: customers take all three for granted. For each one, write whether you do it, they do it, or another tradesman does it.

documenti.titolo: Paperwork, products and IVA in painting and decorating
documenti.intro: A painter doesn't issue system certificates, but a few rules still apply to you. These are the ones that come up most often in work inside the home.

punti.testo: Redoing, repairing and painting interior plaster counts as edilizia libera (free building work, no permit needed), according to the glossary in the DM 2 marzo 2018. For interior painting, as a rule, you don't need to file anything with the Comune (local council).

Outside, in areas with landscape protection, painting needs no permit only if it follows the council's colour plan, if there is one, and keeps the existing features. If it changes them, you may need the simplified landscape authorisation («autorizzazione paesaggistica semplificata», DPR 31/2017). Before changing the colour of a façade, write that the permits are the customer's responsibility.

The D.Lgs. 161/2006 requires the labels on paints and varnishes to state the product subcategory, its limit value and the maximum content of volatile organic compounds. For people with children or allergies, this information matters: naming the product in the quote lets them check it.

Repainting a flat is ordinary maintenance, and on a home IVA is normally 10%. Paints and enamels are not among the beni significativi (significant goods) of the DM 29/12/1999, which is a closed list, so there is no split to make here. If the customer buys the paint at the shop, they pay it with the shop's IVA, and you invoice your own work.

If you repaint an office for a company, or work for the building contractor running the site, painting counts as finishing work on buildings, and the invoice normally goes out without IVA: the customer applies it through the inversione contabile (reverse charge) (DPR 633/1972, art. 17, paragraph 6, and circular 14/E of 2015). The system doesn't calculate it yet: for these jobs, check the total before you send it.

documenti.avvertenza: Take these lines as a guide, not as a consultant's answer. Every job and every customer has its own special cases, and the rules get updated: check with your accountant before you decide.

straniero.titolo: If the customer is a foreigner
straniero.testo: A foreign tenant who has to hand the flat back freshly painted, an owner who lives abroad and freshens up the flat before renting it: they want to know straight away what it costs and what is included. The quote can reach them in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch, with words like «rasatura» or «idropittura» put into their own language, the Italian version being the one that counts, and the withdrawal form translated. You carry on working in Italian.

voci.d: I measure the rooms by eye. How does that become square metres?
voci.r: Say them the way you take them, ‘four and a half by three-eighty’. The system converts the measurement into the unit of your price list item. If a figure it needs for the quantity is missing, like the height, it doesn't make it up and asks you. You see all the quantities before you approve.

voci.d: I measure gross, with no deduction for openings. Will the customer understand that?
voci.r: If you write it down, yes. If you always measure that way, put it in the notice at the bottom of the quote, in your business details: it appears on every PDF. For a single job, write it in the name of the item, for example «idropittura bianca, due mani, vuoto per pieno» (white water-based paint, two coats, measured as solid wall, openings not deducted). The draft notes, on the other hand, stay with you.

voci.d: The mould can come back. How do I write that without scaring the customer?
voci.r: With one plain sentence on the quote, for example that the treatment does not remove the causes of the damp. In the draft, add it to the name of the anti-mould item, or keep it fixed in the notice at the bottom of the quote. The customer doesn't see the draft notes.

voci.d: Is it enough to write «tinteggiatura» (painting), or do I have to say which paint I use?
voci.r: It's better to say. Keep separate items in your price list for breathable, washable, anti-mould and coloured paint: when you say «washable paint in the kitchen», the draft picks that item and the customer sees what they are buying.

voci.d: They're asking me for the façade too. What changes in the quote?
voci.r: The items and the exclusions change. Keep exterior painting in your price list separate from interior painting, and when you describe the job, say who provides the scaffolding and who applies for any permits: if they're not yours, they go under the exclusions.

voci.d: The customer wants two colours in the same room. How do I price it?
voci.r: With an item in your price list for the extra colour, per square metre or as a lump sum per room. When you describe the job, say which wall gets the colour and how big it is: the colour line comes out separate from the white.

voci.d: I'm enamelling the internal doors: do I count them per leaf or with the frame?
voci.r: However you prefer, but keep two items in your price list, leaf only and leaf with frame, because frames take time. When you describe the job, say which of the two you're doing, and the draft picks that one.

meta.titolo: Tiler's quote: tiling, screed, grout
meta.descrizione: You tell us the metres of tiling, screed and skirting as you measured them on the survey: the tiler's quote comes out with the prices from your price list.

piastrellista.riga: Tiling by the square metre, screeds, skirting boards, bathroom wall tiling, taking up the old floor.
piastrellista.h1: Tiler's quote: you say the metres, the draft does the sums with your price list
piastrellista.sottotitolo: Floors, wall tiling, screeds, skirting boards and stairs. You describe the survey with the measurements you took, even by eye: rooms become square metres, the perimeter becomes linear metres, and the prices are only the ones you have entered.

esempio.titolo: Two rooms described, one draft to check
esempio.intro: A kitchen and a bathroom to redo, measured in paces and described on the landing. On the right you see the square metres of floor worked out from the room, the bathroom wall calculated up to two metres, the laying of the customer's porcelain stoneware without supply, and the question about the missing trims.
esempio.lavoro: Kitchen and bathroom, floors and wall tiling
esempio.dettatura: Ecco, sono appena uscito dalla signora Esposito. In cucina tolgo il pavimento vecchio, la stanza è tre e venti per due e settanta, poi rasatura e posa del gres sessanta per sessanta, dritto. Le piastrelle le ha già prese lei, quindi solo posa. Battiscopa su tutto il giro della cucina, una dozzina di metri. In bagno demolisco il rivestimento fino a due metri d'altezza, il bagno è due per uno e ottanta. Il massetto del bagno va rifatto, cinque centimetri più o meno, poi guaina liquida nella doccia e pavimento e rivestimento nuovi. Profili in alluminio sugli spigoli, quanti ancora non lo so, devo vedere il disegno che vuole. Le macerie le porto via io. I sanitari non li tocco, li smonta e rimonta il suo idraulico.

voci.titolo: Typical items in a tiler's quote
voci.intro: Demolition, subfloor, laying and finishing: a floor and wall tiling quote reads in that order. You decide the laying price per square metre for each tile size, and it comes from your price list; a type of laying you've never priced stays to be priced.

righe.nota: Write whether the sub-floor is included: it changes the work and the bags of rubble to carry away.
Wall surface, up to the height of the old tiling. State the height.
With the average thickness in the description: a deep screed isn't worth the same as one a few centimetres thick.
For levelling an old base before tiling, even over the existing floor.
Showers, flush-to-floor shower trays, balconies. With the waterproofing tape on corners and drains.
Specify the size: a 60 by 60 tile and a large slab don't take the same time to lay.

righe.voce: Posa in diagonale o a disegno
righe.nota: A supplement on straight laying, for the extra cuts and the waste.
Bathroom and kitchen. Write whether door and window openings are deducted from the area.
Only if you are the one buying them. Say whether the waste allowance is included in the quantity.
Separate from the cement-based kind: it costs more in material and in time.
Per linear metre. Cut from the same tile or ready-made: write which.
Corners of wall tiling, shower edges, steps.

righe.voce: Posa soglia o davanzale in pietra
righe.nota: Pieces cut to size for doors and windows.
Tread and riser together. Stairs are counted per step, not per square metre.
For drains and connections. On hard porcelain stoneware you need a diamond core bit.
Transport and disposal. If someone else does it, put it under exclusions.

prezzare.titolo: How to price a tiling job
prezzare.intro: The square metre looks like a simple unit, and that's exactly why arguments start: the customer counts the metres of the room, you count the ones to be laid. Here's where it pays to be clear.

punti.testo: For wall tiling, write whether you take door and window openings off the total or not. For floors, whether the metres are the usable floor area or include the space under fixed furniture. It's one sentence and it saves you redoing the sums at the end of the job.

punti.titolo: One line for each type of laying
punti.testo: Large format, thin slabs, mosaic, herringbone or diagonal laying: each one takes its own time. If your price list has only one line, «posa pavimento» (floor laying), you end up giving away the hard job or overcharging for the easy one.

What's under the old floor you only find out when you open it up. Put the screed or the levelling in the quote if you think it will be needed, and write under the items that any unforeseen reworking of the subfloor is charged separately.

It often happens that the customer chooses and buys them. The line then becomes laying only: you say so in your description and the system doesn't add the supply. In the name of the laying item, write who is responsible if the boxes run short or arrive in different shades.

Knocking down the old tiling is one item, taking away the bags is another. If the disposal is yours, put it in as a line; if the customer or the firm that hired you does it, write it under exclusions.

Skirting boards, trims, thresholds, holes for the drains: they're priced by the metre or by the piece, and they're the lines the customer doesn't expect. If you mention them in your account they go into the draft with their unit and you don't have to add them afterwards.

documenti.titolo: Paperwork, rules and VAT for tilers
documenti.intro: You don't need much paperwork to redo a floor, but some, yes. These are the things worth knowing when you prepare a quote for laying tiles in a home.

punti.testo: Repairing, replacing or renewing interior flooring, including membranes and subfloors, and interior wall coverings counts as «edilizia libera» (building work that needs no permit) according to the glossary of the DM 2 marzo 2018. If the tiling is part of a bigger renovation, the paperwork is handled by whoever coordinates the site.

For ceramic tiling on floors and walls there's UNI 11493-1, with instructions for design, laying and maintenance. It isn't a law, but it's the reference for a job done properly: quoting it in your estimate tells the customer how you work.

Redoing a floor or wall tiling in a home is maintenance, with IVA normally at 10%. Tiles are not among the beni significativi (significant goods) of the DM 29/12/1999, so if you supply them they follow the rate of the job with no separate calculation. If in a bathroom you also supply sanitaryware and taps, those are significant goods.

Laying floors in a shop, an office or as a subcontractor for a building contractor is finishing work on a building: normally the inversione contabile (reverse charge) applies (art. 17, paragraph 6, letter a-ter of DPR 633/1972), and the customer applies the IVA. The system doesn't calculate it yet, so in these cases check the total before you send the quote.

Waste from maintenance work is considered produced at the premises of whoever does the job (art. 193, comma 19, of the D.Lgs. 152/2006). For small quantities, transport to your premises can be done with a delivery note («documento di trasporto») instead of the waste transport form («formulario»). Write in the quote whether disposal is included.

documenti.avvertenza: This is general guidance to help you get your bearings, not professional advice: for your own case, ask your accountant or a technician, also because rules and rates change over time.

straniero.titolo: Floors for people who speak another language
straniero.testo: An owner who lives abroad and only drops by to choose the tiles, or someone redoing the bathroom before renting the flat out: they want to understand what they're paying for without an interpreter. The quote can go out in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch, with screed, grout joints and skirting boards translated item by item and the Italian version being the one that counts. You check the items in Italian.

voci.d: I took the measurements of the room, but wall tiling is counted by wall area. What do I do?
voci.r: Give the measurements the way you took them, for example ‘bathroom two metres by one eighty, tiling up to two metres’. The system redoes the sum in the unit of your item, square metres of wall, and you check it line by line before approving.

voci.d: I don't know yet what state the subfloor is in. Do I put it in or not?
voci.r: Put it in as an item if you think it will be needed, or say it as an exclusion: «any redoing of the screed excluded». Exclusions are written out plainly under the items, and the customer reads them before accepting.

voci.d: I have different prices for sixty by sixty and for large format. Does the system tell them apart?
voci.r: Use the items in your price list just as you wrote them. If you say the size when you describe the job, the draft picks the matching item; if it can't find one, the line stays to be priced, highlighted, and you choose.

voci.d: Can I advise the customer to take a few extra boxes?
voci.r: Yes. In the draft, add it to the name of the laying item, for example «piastrelle della cliente, con una scatola in più per i tagli» (the customer's tiles, with one extra box for cuts): that's the text the customer reads on the PDF. If you only say it in your description, it ends up in the notes, which stay with you.

voci.d: I'm working for a contractor who takes away the rubble. How do I remove the disposal?
voci.r: You say «rubble taken away by the contractor». The disposal item doesn't go into the draft and the sentence appears among the exclusions.

voci.d: I count stairs per step. Does the system understand that?
voci.r: Yes, if the item in your price list is per piece. You say «fourteen steps, tread and riser» and the line comes out per step. If you give the measurements in metres instead, the quantity is recalculated in the unit of the item, and you check it before approving.

voci.d: I'm laying over the old floor without demolishing. How do I write that?
voci.r: Keep laying over an existing floor in your price list as its own item, with levelling or primer if needed, and when you describe the job, say that you're not demolishing. That way no demolition line appears, and the customer understands why the price is different from a full redo.

meta.titolo: Builder's quote: partition walls, chases, plastering
meta.descrizione: You describe the demolition, partition walls and plastering you saw on the site visit: the builder's quote comes out with the prices from your price list and questions about what's missing.

muratore.riga: Demolition, partition walls, opening and closing doorways, chases, plastering and skim coats.
muratore.h1: Builder's quote: you describe the work, the prices come from your price list
muratore.sottotitolo: Demolition, partition walls, door openings, chases, plastering, help with the installations. You say what you saw, with measurements taken by pacing or by eye: the draft redoes them in square metres, linear metres or cubic metres, as you have them in your price list, and whatever you haven't said becomes a question.

esempio.titolo: Work said over the phone, lines in the draft
esempio.intro: One partition wall to knock down, one to put up and two doors to move, told to a partner over the phone. On the right you see the square metres of demolition and partition worked out from the measurements, the chases per metre, the customer's door subframe as masonry work only, and the question about the skim coat that can't be measured yet.
esempio.lavoro: Flat, new layout of the rooms
esempio.dettatura: Senti, lavoro del signor Ricci. Tra cucina e soggiorno butto giù il tramezzo, sarà tre e sessanta per due e settanta, forato da otto. Poi ne tiro su uno nuovo in camera per fare la cabina armadio, due e quaranta più o meno, stessa altezza. Apro una porta nuova nel corridoio, con l'architrave, e chiudo quella vecchia del bagno. Tracce per l'elettricista e l'idraulico, una quarantina di metri in tutto, e poi le chiudo io. Intonaco civile sul tramezzo nuovo. In soggiorno c'è da rasare, quanti metri non lo so finché non tolgo la carta da parati. Il controtelaio della porta l'ha già comprato lui, io lo muro e basta. Le macerie le porto via io. La pratica in Comune la fa il suo geometra, non è roba mia.

voci.titolo: Typical items in a builder's quote
voci.intro: Demolishing, building, opening, closing, plastering: the masonry work in a home is written with these lines, almost all per square metre or per metre. You set the price by thickness and material and it comes from your price list; a job you don't have in your price list stays to be priced.

righe.nota: Write the thickness: a thin hollow-brick wall and a solid wall don't come down in the same time.
Stripping back to the brick, before redoing the plaster.
State the thickness of the brick and whether you take the door openings off the total.
Cutting, lintel and finishing the reveals.
Brick infill wall, ready for plastering.
Building in the door subframe. If the client supplies it, the line is fitting only.
For electrical or plumbing systems. Write which system you are cutting it for.
Filling with mortar and making good flush with the wall. Often separate from the cutting.
Scratch coat, base coat and finish. Say whether corner beads on the edges are included.
On old plaster, to leave the wall ready for painting.
Patch repairs, after chases or where plaster has come away. If you apply a minimum charge, write it down.
For the kitchen hood, the air conditioner drain, ventilation. State the diameter.
Support work for the electrician and plumber, when it can't be counted by the metre.
If you count them by volume, say so. Write whether disposal at the tip is included.

prezzare.titolo: How to price a bricklayer's job
prezzare.intro: In masonry work the price depends on things the client can't see: the thickness of the wall, the floor, what you find inside when you open it up. Writing them down is how you avoid having to explain them later.

punti.testo: Partition walls and plastering are counted by the square metre, but the client doesn't know what's inside. Write the thickness, the type of brick and whether openings are deducted. That's a few words and it ends the argument before it starts.

punti.titolo: Demolition also means carrying it down
punti.testo: Demolition includes carrying the bags down to the ground floor, and the haulage. A fourth floor with no lift isn't a ground floor with a yard: put it in the price or on a separate line, but don't leave it unsaid.

Old pipes, beams where you don't expect them, plaster that comes down in pieces. Write under the items that whatever is found when you open up is assessed separately, at the price list rate or by the hour.

Chases, filling, holes: small jobs that add up. Decide whether to count them by the metre, by the piece or by the hour, and write which system they are for, so it's clear they're not inside the electrician's price.
For one patch of plaster or a single hole, the trip costs more than the job. If you have a minimum charge in your price list, the draft uses it; if not, the line is left to be priced and you decide.

Paperwork, calculations, systems, final painting: if you don't do them, put them under exclusions. That's where the client understands that your price is for the masonry work, not for the whole house.

documenti.titolo: Paperwork, safety and IVA in masonry work
documenti.intro: The bricklayer is often the first person on site, and the client also asks them what is needed to get started. These are the things worth knowing.

punti.testo: Moving internal walls or opening internal doors, without touching structural parts, is manutenzione straordinaria (extraordinary maintenance): you need a CILA (comunicazione di inizio lavori asseverata, a notice of works start backed by a technician's sworn statement) (art. 6-bis of DPR 380/2001), with the asseverazione (sworn statement) of a qualified technician and the details of the firm doing the work. If the paperwork isn't yours, write it under exclusions.

Redoing, repairing or painting internal plaster is edilizia libera (free building work, no permit needed) under the glossary of the DM 2 marzo 2018. It also applies to façades, but in areas with a vincolo paesaggistico (landscape protection) the authorisation is not needed only if you respect the existing colours, materials and features.

From 1 October 2024, firms and self-employed workers who physically work on a building site must have the patente a crediti (points-based licence for building sites) (art. 27 of D.Lgs. 81/2008), even if they aren't building firms. The client must check it: keeping the details to hand avoids delays.

Under art. 193, paragraph 19, of D.Lgs. 152/2006, rubble from small building jobs is considered produced at the premises of whoever does the work, and in limited quantities it can be taken there with the transport document. In the quote, write who takes it away and whether disposal is included.

Moving a partition wall or redoing plaster in a home is maintenance, with IVA normally at 10% (art. 7 of legge 488/1999). With a customer who has a partita IVA (VAT number), demolition, plastering and finishing work on a building normally go under the inversione contabile (reverse charge) (art. 17, paragraph 6, of DPR 633/1972), and the same goes for subcontracting for a building contractor. Building a new structure outside a subcontract does not: check with your accountant. Today the system calculates 10% and 22%, not the inversione contabile: in those cases check the total before you send it.

documenti.avvertenza: Take these as a reminder for the trade, not as advice: every site has its own rules, and for permits and invoices the last word belongs to the technician and the accountant.

straniero.titolo: Masonry work for people living abroad
straniero.testo: Someone renovating from far away comes for the site visit and then decides from their own country: they need to understand from the quote which walls come down and what is left out. It can reach them in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch, with «tramezzo» (partition wall) and «rasatura» (skim coat) rendered so the meaning doesn't change, and the Italian version being the one that counts. You read and check it in Italian.

voci.d: Can I describe the job in Romanian or Albanian?
voci.r: Yes. You speak in whichever language comes easiest, and the draft comes out in Italian, with the items from your price list. You check it before it goes out, as always.

voci.d: I measured the partition wall by pacing it out. Is that OK?
voci.r: That's fine. You say ‘three sixty by two seventy’ or ‘about forty metres’, and the system redoes the sum in the unit of your item. Before approving you see every line and correct whatever doesn't add up.

voci.d: I cut the chases for the electrician but the client pays me for them. How do I write them?
voci.r: As your own items, by the metre, and in your description you say which system they are for. If someone else does the filling, say so: it goes under exclusions and you won't find it in the total.

voci.d: The paperwork at the Comune (town council) is done by the client's surveyor. Should I mention it?
voci.r: It's worth it. ‘Pratica edilizia esclusa’ (building paperwork excluded) stops the client thinking it's included in your price. The sentence goes under the items, written plainly.

voci.d: I don't know how much skimming there will be until I take the wallpaper off. What do I put?
voci.r: You don’t put in a random number. The line stays without a quantity and you get the question; when you know, you answer and the total updates. If you want the client to read that anything found later is counted at the price of the item, write it in the notice at the bottom of the quote.

voci.d: At the end of the job the client says ‘this wasn’t there’. How do I protect myself?
voci.r: The client accepts the quote online, and what is kept is the name, date, time and a copy of the PDF they accepted, with the exclusions written under the items. You can also see when they opened it and when they accepted it.

voci.d: Fourth floor, no lift: where do I put the cost of carrying the rubble down?
voci.r: If you have it in your price list as a separate item, say the quantity when you describe the job, ‘three cubic metres to carry down by hand’, and the line comes out with its price. If you keep it inside the demolition price, write it in the item name, so the client knows it’s included.

meta.titolo: Renovation quote for building firms
meta.descrizione: Turnkey bathroom or a whole flat: you describe the site and the building work quote comes out item by item, with the prices from your price list.

impresa.riga: Full renovations, turnkey bathrooms, whole flats, several crews in one quote.
impresa.h1: Renovation quote: the whole site in one draft, with your price list
impresa.sottotitolo: Systems, finishes, windows and doors, site overheads and the work of the crews you coordinate. You describe the site visit room by room: the draft puts the items together with the prices from your price list and asks you about whatever the client hasn't decided yet.

esempio.titolo: A whole job, described out loud
esempio.intro: A turnkey bathroom, a bedroom and the site costs, summed up by the owner on the way out. On the right you can see the work of several crews put into a single draft, the skip on its own line, the client’s taps and fittings as fitting only, and questions about what the clients haven’t decided yet.
esempio.dettatura: Ricapitolo il cantiere della famiglia Moretti. Bagno chiavi in mano: impianto idraulico nuovo, pavimento e rivestimenti, il bagno è circa due e mezzo per due. Piatto doccia a filo, vaso e bidet sospesi. La rubinetteria l'ha scelta e comprata la signora, noi la montiamo. In camera tinteggiamo pareti e soffitto, una cinquantina di metri. Cambiamo la finestra della camera, una e venti per uno e quaranta. Cassone per le macerie in cortile, è un terzo piano senza ascensore. Cambiamo anche le porte interne delle altre stanze, laccate bianche: quante non l'hanno ancora deciso. Il condizionatore lo fa il loro tecnico, è escluso.

voci.titolo: Typical items in a renovation quote
voci.intro: As well as the crews’ work, a building firm writes down the site costs and its own management: these are the lines the client compares most between two offers. Selling prices are yours and come from your price list; a job that isn’t in your price list stays to be priced.

righe.nota: Access, protection, temporary connections, equipment. You put it in once, at the start.
On its own line, so the customer sees them and doesn't mix them up with your margin.
Stairs, lift, the building's entrance hall: dust sheets, cardboard, cleaning during the works.
With transport and emptying. If you need to occupy public land, write who applies for the permit.
The turnkey item: list in the item name what it includes, so the lump sum isn’t a mystery.
Bathroom or kitchen, done by your crew or by a plumber you trust: for the customer it is one line.
Whole flat or individual rooms, with the installer's dichiarazione di conformità (declaration of conformity).
For IVA they count as beni significativi (significant goods) in maintenance work: see below.
When the customer buys the taps and fittings: fitting only.
Say which type: hinged, sliding into the wall, lacquered, hollow-core.

righe.voce: Fornitura e posa pavimenti e rivestimenti
righe.nota: With the price band of the material you allowed for: it is the customer's choice that changes the total most.
Write how many coats and whether skim coats are included.
Windows and French windows. A bene significativo (significant good) for IVA: keep it on a separate line.
Your work as director: orders, crews, timing, site visits. If you charge for it, give it a line.
Building permit paperwork, site supervision, safety coordinator. If the customer pays for them separately, they go under exclusions.
The big clean before you hand back the keys.

prezzare.intro: On a job with several trades the risk is not getting one price wrong, it is forgetting a line. The customer compares your total with another firm's, and whoever wrote down better what is in and what is not wins.

punti.testo: The customer wants one number, and that's fine. But underneath, keep the individual jobs: when halfway through the customer changes the tile or drops the bath, you work on one line and not on the whole quote.

Site set-up, protection, skip, cleaning, safety costs. Hidden inside the single items they push up every price with no explanation; on their own lines the customer understands they are site costs, not mark-ups.

If the plumber and the electrician are tradesmen you trust, what you pay them is not the price for the customer: it includes your coordination and your guarantee. In your price list keep the selling price, not the buying price.

Floors, sanitaryware, doors: the client often chooses them once work has started. Write the range or model you allowed for, and underneath the items say that a different choice changes the price of that line, not of everything else.

punti.titolo: What is left out of the contract
punti.testo: Surveyor, paperwork, furniture, appliances, air conditioners: in a renovation the list of what is not included matters as much as the list of what is. Written under the items, it avoids the classic «I thought that was included».

How many doors to replace, shower or bath, the colour of the walls: if the client hasn’t decided, the system doesn’t make up a number. You get a question about the quantity, or it ends up in the notes for you, to sort out before approving. Better to leave something open than to put a made-up number inside a total.

documenti.titolo: Paperwork, safety and IVA on a renovation job
documenti.intro: When the firm takes on all the work, the customer expects it to know what is needed before, during and after. These are the things that come up most often in home renovations.

punti.testo: Moving walls or opening internal doors without touching the structure is extraordinary maintenance (manutenzione straordinaria) with a CILA (notification of start of works, art. 6-bis of DPR 380/2001); for heavier work the surveyor says which permit applies. The notification must include the details of the firm carrying out the work: make clear in the quote who hires and pays the surveyor.

punti.titolo: Several firms on the same site
punti.testo: If several firms work on site, even at different times, the client must appoint the safety coordinator (art. 90 of D.Lgs. 81/2008) and send the preliminary notification (art. 99). With a single firm the notification is needed from 200 man-days upwards. Saying so up front stops the customer finding out once work has begun.

punti.titolo: Patente a crediti, also for the people you bring in
punti.testo: You and the firms or tradesmen working on site must hold the patente a crediti (points-based licence for construction sites, art. 27 of D.Lgs. 81/2008), apart from the exclusions provided. The client checks it for subcontractors too, so it pays to have everyone's details ready.

In private building work worth at or above the threshold set by DM 143/2021, before the final payment you need the attestazione di congruità (certificate of labour cost congruity) of the workforce, issued by the Cassa Edile (building workers’ fund) at the request of the main contractor or the client. On big sites, take it into account when you set the final payment.

If the customer claims tax deductions for works above the threshold in legge 234/2021 (art. 1, comma 43-bis), the contract must state that the building work is carried out applying the collective agreements of the building sector, and the statement must also appear on the invoice. Without that sentence in the contract the customer risks losing the relief.

On a full site, how the work is classed decides the IVA. If it is ordinary or extraordinary maintenance of a home, 10% applies up to the limit of the beni significativi (significant goods) of DM 29/12/1999, which include sanitaryware and taps, windows and doors, boilers and air conditioners: the draft asks you for the value of each item marked and splits between 10% and 22%. If the technician has classed it as restauro, risanamento conservativo or ristrutturazione edilizia (restoration, conservative renovation or building renovation), the contract goes at 10% without that calculation. Invoices from your building subcontractors reach you with inversione contabile (reverse charge); if instead you are the one working as a subcontractor, the system doesn’t calculate it yet, so check the total before sending it.

documenti.avvertenza: This is a summary so you don't forget anything, not technical or tax advice: on your job, the designer, the coordinator and your accountant decide, and these rules are updated often.

straniero.titolo: A site for a client from abroad
straniero.testo: Someone who lives abroad and buys a home here looks for a firm that takes on the whole site, because they can’t coordinate crews from far away. They need a single quote that they can understand line by line: in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch, with charges and work translated, the Italian version being the one that counts and the withdrawal form in their language. They accept it from the link, without having to come and sign.

voci.d: An outside plumber and electrician are working on the site. Do their items go in my quote?
voci.r: Yes, if you are the one with the contract with the customer. Put their jobs in your price list at your selling price: when you describe the bathroom, those lines go in with the others, and the customer gets one single quote.

voci.d: The customer wants a turnkey price for the bathroom. Can I keep just one item?
voci.r: Yes, if you have the lump-sum item in your price list. Write in the item name what it includes and what it doesn’t, so the client doesn’t imagine more inside than what you put in.

voci.d: Should I put the safety costs on a separate line?
voci.r: You can keep them as a fixed item in your price list and mention them when you describe the job, «plus the oneri della sicurezza (safety costs)». A separate line shows the customer what they are paying for, and the rest of the items don't look inflated.

voci.d: The customer still has to choose the floors and sanitaryware. Should I still do the quote?
voci.r: Yes. You say what you allowed for, for example ‘mid-range porcelain stoneware, standard wall-hung sanitaryware’, and you check that it’s in the item names: that’s what the client reads on the PDF. The notes on the draft stay with you. If a quantity is missing, it comes back to you as a question and you fill it in when the client decides.

voci.d: Extraordinary maintenance or renovation: who decides what I answer to the system?
voci.r: The classification comes from the building permit (titolo edilizio), so ask the technician who handles the paperwork. Then answer the question about the type of work: with renovation the IVA comes out at 10% without the calculation of the beni significativi (significant goods), with maintenance the draft asks you for the value of the windows and sanitaryware marked in your price list.

voci.d: Other firms are coming onto the site. Do I have to tell the client in the quote?
voci.r: It’s a good idea. With more than one firm, the client has to appoint the safety coordinator and send the preliminary notification: if you’re not taking care of it, say so as an exclusion when you describe the job, ‘safety coordinator paid for by the client’.

voci.d: Does the quote go out with the firm's logo?
voci.r: Yes, the PDF carries your logo. The customer gets it with a link to accept it online, and you can see when they open it and when they accept it.

meta.titolo: Plumbing and heating quote, boilers and air conditioning
meta.descrizione: The plumbing and heating quote for boilers, radiators and air conditioners: you describe the job after the site visit and the draft uses only the prices from your price list.

termoidraulico.riga: Boilers, radiators, thermostatic valves, split air conditioners and heat pumps.
termoidraulico.h1: Plumbing and heating quote: boiler, radiators and air conditioning in one draft
termoidraulico.sottotitolo: Boiler replacement, radiators, thermostatic valves, splits and refrigerant lines. You describe the site visit the way you would to your mate on the job: the draft takes its prices only from your price list, keeps the heat source separate from the rest and asks you about whatever you haven't counted.

esempio.titolo: A site visit described, a draft to check
esempio.intro: A house with a boiler to replace, a few radiators and two air conditioners. On the right you can see the boiler on its own line, separate from the flue and the flushing, the metres of air-con pipework, the client’s programmable thermostat as connection only and the question about the thermostatic valves to count.
esempio.lavoro: Boiler, radiators and two splits, house
esempio.dettatura: Bene, casa Fontana, villetta su due piani. La caldaia vecchia la smonto e ne metto una a condensazione, stessa posizione in cucina, con lo scarico fumi nuovo: saranno quattro metri di tubo. Prima di attaccarla faccio il lavaggio dell'impianto, che è pieno di fanghi. Al piano di sopra cambio i radiatori, sono cinque. Quelli di sotto li tengo, ma ci metto le valvole termostatiche su tutti: quanti sono di preciso devo ricontarli. Il cronotermostato l'ha comprato lui, io lo collego e basta. Poi due split, uno in camera e uno in soggiorno, con il motore esterno sul balcone, una dozzina di metri di linea in tutto. Le tracce per le linee del clima le fa il muratore, e la vecchia canna fumaria sul tetto non la tocco.

voci.titolo: The typical items in a plumbing and heating quote
voci.intro: Boiler, boiler fittings, radiators and air-con lines: a heating quote stands on these lines. The prices are from your price list, and an accessory you’ve never put in your price list stays to be priced.

righe.nota: Including disconnecting the gas, water and flue. It's best to write the disposal as a separate line.

righe.voce: Caldaia a condensazione, fornitura e posa
righe.nota: The boiler is a bene significativo (significant good) for IVA: keep it on its own line, separate from the accessories.
Coaxial or twin pipe, with bends and terminal. Priced per metre, so a long run shows up.
A condensing boiler needs one: if there's no drain nearby, say so up front.
Cleaning the pipes and radiators before fitting the new boiler, with the product specified.
On the boiler return. Many customers don't know what it is: a clear line helps.
Taking off the old one and fitting the new one on the same connections. State the type of radiator included.
Valve body and head, one per radiator. The bathroom and the room with the thermostat usually go without.
Only connection and programming when the customer buys the unit.
For manifold or underfloor systems: with the number of ways written in the item.
Indoor and outdoor unit. This too is a bene significativo (significant good) for IVA.
Insulated, with the connecting cable. Write how many metres are already included in the fitting.
For the air conditioning line or for the flue. Through reinforced concrete it's a different matter: price it separately.
Wall-mounted or floor-standing. If you need platforms or scaffolding to fit them, those are extra.
After working on the boiler's gas line.
Check, cleaning and combustion analysis, with the system paperwork filled in.
When you change the boiler or add an appliance. If it's included, say so.

prezzare.titolo: How to price a plumbing and heating job
prezzare.intro: In heating and air conditioning the value of the job often sits in a single appliance, and the rest looks like filler. But the filler is exactly what the customer doesn't expect to pay for, so it has to be written down.

punti.titolo: The boiler on its own line
punti.testo: Boiler or air conditioner on one side, fitting and accessories on the other. The customer compares the price of the appliance with what they see online, and if it's all lumped together they think you've added a markup. On top of that, for IVA you need them kept apart.
Flue, condensate, flushing, magnetic filter, gas tightness test: these are the items that make the difference between two quotes that look the same. Put them all in, even the ones you do cheaply.

Fitting a split usually includes a certain number of metres of line. Write how many, and keep the extra metre in your price list: when the outdoor unit goes on the other side of the house, the sum is done without arguing.

punti.titolo: Radiators: each, with the type written down
punti.testo: An aluminium radiator, a steel one and a towel rail don't cost the same. Write the type and height included in the item, so that if the customer chooses something different it becomes a variation and not a row.

The client finds the air conditioner or the thermostat on offer and only asks you to fit it. The line becomes installation only, and it’s a good idea to write in the item name that the warranty and after-sales service of the unit stay between them and whoever sold it to them.
The annual service has a fixed price, a breakdown doesn't. Keep the two separate in your price list: the service per unit, fault-finding by the hour plus the call-out, and spare parts on top.

documenti.titolo: Regulations, logbook and IVA for boilers and air conditioners
documenti.intro: In heating and air conditioning the paperwork is not a detail: some of it the customer needs for inspections, some of it you need to work legally. Here's what comes up in home jobs.

punti.testo: Heating, air conditioning and gas systems fall under DM 37/2008: at the end of the job you issue the dichiarazione di conformità (declaration of conformity) with the report on the materials. A design by a registered professional is needed, among other cases, for air conditioning from 40,000 frigories/hour up, for gas systems over 50 kW of thermal input and for those with branched shared flues.

Every heating system must have the libretto di impianto (system logbook) for air conditioning, following the model in the DM 10 febbraio 2014. During checks and servicing you also fill in the energy efficiency inspection report (rapporto di controllo di efficienza energetica) required by DPR 74/2013, for heating over 10 kW and summer cooling over 12 kW.

To install, service or dismantle air conditioners and heat pumps with fluorinated gases you need both the person's certificate and the firm's (DPR 146/2018). Every job must be reported to the Banca dati F-gas (F-gas database) within 30 days.

punti.titolo: IVA on boilers and air conditioners
punti.testo: Replacing the boiler in a home is maintenance, at 10%, but boilers and air conditioners are beni significativi (significant goods, DM 29/12/1999): the 10% on the item applies up to the value of the rest of the work, and the excess goes at 22%. If the item is marked as a significant good in your price list, the draft asks you how much the appliance is worth and splits the IVA using that figure. If you replace just one component, such as the burner, according to the Agenzia delle Entrate (Revenue Agency, circular 15/E of 2018) it counts as part of the price of the service.

Installing an air-to-air air conditioner under 12 kW is normally edilizia libera (work that needs no permit), according to the glossary of the DM 2 marzo 2018. Above that power, or on a protected building, check with a technician. In an area with a landscape restriction (vincolo paesaggistico), an outdoor unit visible from the street or from public space may need the simplified landscape authorisation (autorizzazione paesaggistica semplificata; DPR 31/2017, allegato B, item B.7). If in doubt, write in the quote that permits are the client’s responsibility.

punti.titolo: Boilers and air conditioning for businesses
punti.testo: If you install heating or air conditioning at a company’s premises, between parties with a partita IVA (VAT number) the inversione contabile (reverse charge) normally applies: no IVA on the invoice, the client applies it. Today the system calculates the 10%, the 22% and the split of the beni significativi (significant goods); it doesn’t calculate the inversione contabile yet, so for these jobs check the total before sending it.

documenti.avvertenza: What you read here is a checklist so you don't forget anything, not advice from a technician or a tax adviser. Thresholds, forms and rates change: the rules in force and your commercialista (accountant) decide on the actual case.

straniero.testo: Someone with a second home who wants air-con before the summer, or the family who came over for work and finds at the first winter that the boiler needs replacing: for a plumber and heating engineer these are frequent calls. The quote can go out in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch, with the boiler, accessories and maintenance explained in their language, the Italian version being the one that counts and the withdrawal form translated. You check it in Italian.

domande.titolo: Questions from heating and plumbing engineers

voci.d: I'm replacing a boiler. How do I keep the appliance separate from the rest of the job?
voci.r: If the boiler is an item of its own in your price list, in the draft it comes out on a line separate from the installation, the flue and the accessories. If you mark it as a bene significativo (significant good), the draft asks you how much the boiler is worth and splits the IVA between 10% and 22% when needed. Checking with your accountant is still up to you.

voci.d: Do I have to put the notification to the Banca dati F-gas (F-gas database) in the quote?
voci.r: It’s your obligation, not a service to sell, but it’s worth mentioning: keep it in your price list as a lump-sum item, even at zero price if it’s included, and mention it when you describe the job. That way the client sees the split unit is installed properly.

voci.d: The split installation includes a few metres of pipe run. What if more are needed?
voci.r: Keep two items in your price list: the installation and the extra metre of pipe run. You say how many metres are needed, even roughly, and in the draft you find the per-metre line with the quantity you gave. Before approving, check the quantity: if some of the metres are already in the installation, you correct it.

voci.d: I'm only replacing the burner or the boiler pump. Should it be treated like a new boiler?
voci.r: No. For the Agenzia delle Entrate (the Italian Revenue Agency), a component replaced on an appliance that is already installed falls within the price of the service, without the beni significativi (significant goods) rule. Keep spare parts in your price list as normal items, not marked as beni significativi, and the draft treats them accordingly.

voci.d: Do I count radiators by the piece or by the section?
voci.r: As you have them in your price list. If your item is per piece, the draft counts the radiators. If you also have items by type and height, say so when you tell it about the job and the system looks for the right one. If it can't find it, the line is left to be priced.

voci.d: I do a lot of annual servicing. Does it make sense to use it for that too?
voci.r: Yes, especially when the service turns up extra work: thermostatic valves, a magnetic filter, an expansion vessel to replace. You say so as soon as you've finished the check and the customer gets the quote with your logo while they still remember what you talked about.

voci.d: I send the quote for the boiler and the customer doesn't reply. Can I tell if they've read it?
voci.r: Yes. You can see when the customer opens the quote and when they accept it from the link. If they've opened it and not accepted, you know it's time to call them.

meta.titolo: Plasterboard fitter's quote: walls and ceilings
meta.descrizione: The plasterboard fitter's quote for walls, wall linings, suspended ceilings and insulation: you describe the site visit and the draft uses only the prices from your price list.

cartongessista.riga: Partition walls, wall linings, suspended ceilings, bulkheads and insulation in boards.
cartongessista.h1: Plasterboard fitter's quote: you give the measurements, the draft counts the square metres
cartongessista.sottotitolo: Walls, wall linings, suspended ceilings, bulkheads, insulation. After the site visit you tell it the measurements as you took them, roughly: the draft converts them into the unit of your items, uses only the prices from your price list and asks you about whatever the customer hasn't decided yet.

esempio.titolo: Measurements said out loud, lines in the draft
esempio.intro: An open-plan space to divide, a bathroom with exposed pipes and a bedroom that hears the neighbours. On the right you can see the double-board partition in square metres, the client’s door subframe as fitting only, the holes for the spotlights counted per piece and the question about the bulkheads the client hasn’t decided yet.
esempio.lavoro: Dividing an open-plan space, bathroom and bedroom
esempio.dettatura: Vado col lavoro del signor Rinaldi, appartamento. Il soggiorno lo dividiamo: parete in cartongesso fra soggiorno e studio, quattro e venti per due e settanta, doppia lastra con la lana di roccia dentro. Nella parete va la porta scorrevole, il controtelaio l'ha già comprato lui, io lo inserisco. In bagno una controparete per chiudere i tubi, un metro e ottanta per tutta l'altezza, con la lastra idrorepellente. In corridoio controsoffitto ribassato, saranno una decina di metri quadri, con sei fori per i faretti. Sulla parete della camera che confina con i vicini una controparete isolante, tre e sessanta per due e settanta. In soggiorno le velette per le tende, quante finestre non l'ha ancora deciso. Stuccatura dei giunti compresa, la pittura no, e i faretti li monta l'elettricista.

voci.titolo: Typical items in a plasterboard fitter's quote
voci.intro: With plasterboard the price depends on how many boards, what frame and what insulation: that’s why the lines are told apart by build-up, plus bulkheads, reinforcements and holes. The square-metre price of each type of wall is yours and comes from your price list; a build-up that isn’t in your price list stays to be priced.

righe.voce: Parete divisoria in cartongesso, lastra singola
righe.nota: Metal frame and one board per side. Write the thickness of the frame.

righe.voce: Parete divisoria in cartongesso, doppia lastra
righe.nota: Two boards per side: stiffer, holds weight better and insulates more against noise.
Set away from the wall: leaves room for pipes, cables and insulation.
Flat, on a hung frame. Write the drop height included.
Rock wool or glass wool, with the thickness written in the item.
For bathrooms and kitchens. Keeping it as a supplement makes the reason for the price clear.

righe.voce: Maggiorazione lastra per protezione al fuoco
righe.nota: For service shafts, boiler rooms, ducts. State the type of board.
For curtains, indirect lighting, beams to hide. By the linear metre.
Opening in the wall with reinforced studs for the frame.
Fitting only, if the customer buys the door subframe.

righe.voce: Rinforzo per pensili e carichi sospesi
righe.nota: Where shelves, wall units, TV or wall-hung sanitaryware will go: it has to be decided before closing up.
Just the hole: the connection is the electrician's job.
To reach valves, manifolds or air conditioning units in the ceiling.
On the corners of bulkheads, niches and walls, before jointing.
Write the finish level: ready for paint, or just the joints filled.
With taking away the removed material, if included.

prezzare.titolo: How to price a plasterboard job
prezzare.intro: A price per square metre of plasterboard says little if you don't say what's inside: how many boards, what frame, what insulation, what finish. Two quotes with the same price per metre can be two different jobs.
