punti.testo: Frame depth, number of boards per side, type of board, insulation. Write it in the item name: that’s what the client reads on the PDF and uses to compare your price with someone else’s.

A wall with a door opening isn't counted like a solid wall: either you deduct the opening and charge for it as a separate item, or you count the whole wall as if it were solid. Whichever method you use, write it down, because it's the first thing that gets re-measured.

Filling the joints and handing over a wall ready to paint are not the same job. If someone else does the painting, write how far you go, so the decorator doesn't find any surprises and the customer doesn't call you.

A wall-mounted TV, kitchen wall units, a wall-hung basin: in a plasterboard wall you need reinforcements fitted before closing up. Ask the customer where they'll go and add the item: afterwards it costs twice the effort.

Bulkheads, niches and channels for LEDs are per-metre jobs with lots of cuts. Keep them separate from the square metres of wall or ceiling, otherwise a quote full of details looks the same as one for straight walls.

Wiring and pipes in the walls, spotlights, painting: usually these aren't yours. Put them in the exclusions with the name of whoever does them. The client sees who to call, and you know what to wait for before you close up the boards.

documenti.titolo: Paperwork, boards, IVA and waste in plasterboard work
documenti.intro: Plasterboard changes the layout of a home, so a few rules need keeping in mind. These are the ones that come up again and again in home jobs.

punti.testo: Building or moving non-load-bearing internal walls counts as extraordinary maintenance (DPR 380/2001, art. 3). Usually you need a CILA (communicazione di inizio lavori asseverata, a notice of works start). The client files it with the Comune (town council) together with a technician's sworn statement, and it includes the details of the firm doing the work. If you don't handle the paperwork, write it in the exclusions.

Installing, repairing or replacing a non-structural suspended ceiling is edilizia libera (free building work, no permit needed), according to the glossary of the DM 2 marzo 2018. In home jobs this is the most common case.

Plasterboard follows the standard UNI EN 520, which sets out the types: standard, reduced water absorption, better fire performance and others. Writing the type in the quote stops the client comparing a standard board with a water-resistant one.

A wall or a suspended ceiling in a home normally counts as maintenance, with IVA at 10%. Boards, profiles and insulation are not among the beni significativi (significant goods) of DM 29/12/1999: even if you supply them, there is no split between 10% and 22% to make.

If you work with plasterboard, you are often called in by the firm that has won the job, or you divide up the space in an office. On a building subcontract, or for a client with a partita IVA (VAT number) on a building, the inversione contabile (reverse charge; DPR 633/1972, art. 17, comma 6) usually applies and the invoice goes out without IVA. With a private client it doesn't. The system currently calculates 10% and 22%, not yet the inversione contabile: in these cases check the total before sending it.

Waste from maintenance work and small building jobs is treated as produced at the premises of whoever does the work (D.Lgs. 152/2006, art. 193, comma 19). It's worth having one line for transport and disposal: the client knows that offcuts and old boards won't be left in the cellar.

documenti.avvertenza: These are guidance notes, not advice from a technician or an accountant. Paperwork and tax rules depend on the case and on the Comune: before you put them in a real quote, have them checked by whoever handles them.

straniero.titolo: If the client speaks another language
straniero.testo: A foreigner who buys an open-plan flat and wants to make a bedroom out of it, or a foreign company dividing up an office: «controparete» (lining wall) and «veletta» (bulkhead) mean nothing to them. The quote can go out in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch, with these words explained clearly, the Italian version as the one that counts and the withdrawal form translated. You prepare it and check it in Italian.

voci.d: In my price list I have the single-layer board wall, but here I'm doing a double layer. What happens?
voci.r: If the double layer isn't there, the line stays unpriced and is highlighted: the system doesn't put the single-layer price in place of the double. You write the price yourself and add the item to your price list.

voci.d: I hand over the joints filled but not the wall ready to paint. How do I write that?
voci.r: With two items in your price list, joint filling and full skim coat, and you say in your account which one you're doing. If the paint and the final skim are done by someone else, say so: they end up in the exclusions under the items.

voci.d: I often work for a firm that passes me its jobs. Do I still need it?
voci.r: Yes, there too you need a clear quote, item by item. Watch out for IVA: between firms in the trade the inversione contabile (reverse charge) usually applies, and the system doesn't calculate it yet. Check the total with your accountant before sending it.

voci.d: The client wants to hang the TV on the new wall. What do I put in the quote?
voci.r: The reinforcement, per metre or per piece, as you have it in your price list. Say it in your account with the position, «reinforcement for the TV on the living room wall», so it goes into the draft before the boards are closed up.

voci.d: There's a door in the wall. Do I take the opening off the square metres?
voci.r: It's up to you, but be consistent with the door opening item. If you keep the opening as a separate item, correct the wall's square metres in the draft by taking off the opening. If you count full for empty, write it in the name of the item.

voci.d: Above the suspended ceiling there's the air-conditioning unit. How do I allow for the access hatch?
voci.r: With a «botola d'ispezione» (access hatch) item, priced per piece, in your price list. Mention it in your account together with the suspended ceiling: the air-conditioning engineer will find it, and the client already knows why it's there.

voci.d: The client asks how much the lining wall cuts out noise. What do I write?
voci.r: Write the build-up in the name of the item: frame, number of boards, type and thickness of the insulation. Don't promise decibels without a measurement: the client compares the package, and on that you're on safe ground.

meta.titolo: Window fitter's quote: windows and roller shutters
meta.descrizione: You say the measurements and models of windows, shutters and security doors: the window fitter's quote comes out with the prices from your price list and the IVA on window and door frames.

serramentista.riga: Windows, French windows, hinged shutters, roller shutters, security doors, removal of the old ones and fitting.
serramentista.h1: Window fitter's quote: measurements and models by voice, prices from your price list
serramentista.sottotitolo: Windows, French windows, hinged shutters, roller shutters and security doors. You describe the survey opening by opening, just as you noted it on your pad: the draft takes the prices from your price list, keeps apart the parts that have to be kept apart for IVA, and asks you for whatever is missing.

esempio.titolo: The survey said out loud, the draft to check
esempio.intro: Four PVC windows to replace, with new roller shutters and a security door the clients have already bought. On the right you see each window on one line with its measurements, the roller shutters separate from the frames, the security door as fitting only, and the question about insect screens.
esempio.dettatura: Rilievo dai signori Marchetti. Cambiamo tutte le finestre, PVC bianco, doppio vetro basso emissivo. In cucina finestra a due ante, uno e venti per uno e quaranta. In soggiorno la portafinestra a due ante, uno e quaranta per due e venti circa. Le due camere hanno finestre a un'anta, ottanta per uno e trenta. La vasistas del bagno la lasciano. Smontaggio delle vecchie in legno e smaltimento, ci penso io. Tapparelle nuove in alluminio coibentato su tutte, con il motore solo in soggiorno. Le zanzariere le vogliono, ma su quante finestre non l'hanno ancora deciso. La porta blindata d'ingresso l'hanno già comprata loro, io la monto e basta. Le opere murarie sui davanzali non sono mie, le fa il loro muratore.

voci.titolo: Typical items in a window fitter's quote
voci.intro: Frame, shading, removal, fitting and finishing: when you replace windows, these lines are kept separate, also for IVA. The price of each model is yours and comes from your price list. A profile system that isn't in your price list stays unpriced.

righe.nota: With the opening measurements and the glazing included: it's what the client compares between two quotes.
State the profile system and the type of glass, not just the material.
Say whether the low threshold is included.
Bathrooms and utility rooms. Also in tilt-and-turn version.

righe.voce: Serramento in alluminio a taglio termico
righe.nota: For glazed walls and non-standard sizes, per square metre of opening.
With or without the old frame left in the wall: say which, because it changes the job.
Wood, glass and ironmongery to take away. If the client does it, it goes in the exclusions.
New, or reusing the existing one: decide at the survey, because it changes the fitting.
For windows and doors supplied by others: fixings, sealants and joint tapes.
Per square metre of fabric. For IVA it isn't added to the value of the window or door.
Tubular motor with control. Say whether the electrician does the electrical connection.
Hinged, with the hinges fixed into the wall. State the colour and whether the slats are fixed or adjustable.
The roller shutter box is often where the cold gets in.
Vertical for windows, side-opening for French windows.
State the burglar-resistance class and the cladding panel: they're the first things the client asks about.
Fitting only, when the customer has bought the door themselves.
Finishing between the frame and the wall, inside the house.
Sashes that rub, hardware that won't close: charged by the hour.

prezzare.titolo: How to price a window fitter's job
prezzare.intro: With windows and doors, the customer compares quotes that have the same name but different contents. The way not to lose the job on price is to show what is inside each line.

punti.testo: The quote is based on the measurements taken at the survey. Write on the quote that the final measurements are checked before the order: a window that's a few centimetres out can't be sent back.
Profile, glass, hardware, colour. Two ‘PVC’ windows can be two different products: in the price list item, write the system, the glazing and the colour, so the customer compares like with like.

These are the three lines that separate a complete quote from one that only looks cheaper. Always include them, or write clearly that they aren't there and who deals with them. If in your account you only say «I'll take them away myself», disposal stays included in the removal: if you want it on its own line, say how many windows you dispose of.

punti.titolo: Separate parts on their own lines
punti.testo: Roller shutters, shutters, fly screens: on separate lines the customer understands what they are paying for, and you need them for the IVA (Italian VAT) too, because their value is not added to that of the windows.

punti.titolo: Doors and windows bought by the client
punti.testo: Security doors or windows bought by the customer: the line becomes fitting only. Write what it includes (removing the old one, fixings, adjustment) and that you are not responsible for the quality of the product.
Window sills, reveals, plaster around the frame: if you don't do them, put them under exclusions. It's what the customer finds out on fitting day if nobody wrote it down for them.

documenti.titolo: CE marking, fitting, IVA and tax deductions
documenti.intro: People who change their windows ask about paperwork and tax deductions even before they ask about colour. Here is what you need to know to answer well and to write it correctly in the quote.

punti.titolo: CE marking and declaration of performance
punti.testo: Windows and external pedestrian doors must carry the CE mark under the harmonised standard UNI EN 14351-1 (EU Regulation 305/2011), with the declaration of performance (DoP). You hand the customer the DoP, the CE label and the maintenance instructions: they are also needed for the tax deduction paperwork.

UNI 11673-1 sets out the criteria for designing the fitting of windows and doors, joints included, and UNI 11673-2 describes the skills of the fitter. They are voluntary standards: they become binding if you refer to them in the contract. Mentioning them in the quote tells the customer how you fit.

Replacing the windows in a home is usually maintenance, at 10%, but external and internal frames are beni significativi (significant goods, DM 29/12/1999): the 10% applies to their value only up to the value of the rest of the work, and the part above that goes at 22%. According to circolare 15/E of 2018, roller shutters, shutters, Venetian blinds and insect screens have functional autonomy and are not added to the window, unless they are built into the frame.

punti.titolo: Windows and doors for companies and firms
punti.testo: If you fit windows supplied by others for a firm or in an office, the fitting alone is finishing work and usually goes under inversione contabile (reverse charge; art. 17, comma 6, lettera a-ter of DPR 633/1972). If instead you sell the window with the fitting, it's a supply of goods and the reverse charge doesn't apply. The system currently calculates 10%, 22% and the split of the beni significativi (significant goods), not the inversione contabile: for fitting only for a firm, check the total before sending it.

Repairing, replacing or renewing external windows and doors counts as edilizia libera (building work that needs no permit) under the glossary of the DM 2 marzo 2018. In areas with a vincolo paesaggistico (landscape protection restriction), no authorisation is needed only if you keep to the existing materials, finishes and features: if the customer wants to change colour or material, it must be checked first.

If the customer asks for the energy-saving deduction, the work's data sheet must be sent to ENEA within 90 days of the end of the work. It needs the asseverazione (sworn technical statement) of a technician or, for a single dwelling, the certification of the supplier or installer. Write in the quote whether you take care of it.

documenti.avvertenza: These are working notes to help you find your way, not professional advice: rates, deductions and rules change often, and for a real case your accountant and the technician decide.

straniero.testo: The owner of a second home who lives abroad wants to close it up properly before winter and compares quotes from a distance, looking at glass, profile and colour. The quote reaches him in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch, with the opening measurements unchanged, the explanation of the beni significativi (significant goods) in his language, the Italian version as the one that counts and the withdrawal form translated.

voci.d: In my price list some windows are priced per piece and others per square metre. Does the system get confused?
voci.r: No. The measurements you give are reworked into the unit of each item: if the item is per square metre, the system does the sum; if it is per piece, it counts the pieces. Before approving, you check line by line.

voci.d: How do I split the IVA between windows, roller shutters and fitting?
voci.r: In your price list you mark the window items as beni significativi (significant goods), not the roller shutters and insect screens. When you answer the three questions about the job (home, type of work, who buys the materials), the draft asks you how much the window is worth on each marked line and splits between 10% and 22%, with a warning to check with your accountant.

voci.d: I take the final measurements after acceptance. Can I write that?
voci.r: Yes. Put it in the notice at the bottom of the quote, in your business details: «measurements to be checked before the order». It appears on every PDF and the client accepts it along with the rest. The notes in the draft, on the other hand, stay with you.

voci.d: The client wants the energy-saving tax relief. What do I write in the quote?
voci.r: Write in the name of the items the data needed for the paperwork, such as the thermal transmittance of the window, and say in your account who sends the form to ENEA. If you don't deal with it, it goes into the exclusions.

voci.d: Do I keep the old subframe or replace it: how do I write it?
voci.r: With two items in your price list, keeping the old one and a new subframe, and in your account you say which one you're doing on which openings. If you only decide after taking the window out, say so: the line stays without a quantity and asks you for it.

voci.d: The windows are made to the client's measurements. Can they still withdraw?
voci.r: For made-to-measure goods there is usually no right of withdrawal, but that doesn't hold if the contract comes from a visit of yours that wasn't requested, and the fitting remains a service. The withdrawal form is on the acceptance page anyway; the guide on [withdrawing from a quote accepted at home](/guide/recesso-preventivo-accettato-a-casa) explains the cases.

voci.d: I sell and fit windows for a company's premises. Does the invoice go without IVA?
voci.r: Usually not: if you sell the window and the fitting is incidental, it's a supply of goods and you charge the IVA, at 22% if it isn't a home. The inversione contabile (reverse charge) only covers fitting alone of windows supplied by others.

meta.titolo: Joiner's quote by voice, from your own price list
meta.descrizione: The joinery quote comes from your own account: built-in wardrobes, interior doors, stairs and fitting, with the prices from your price list. The customer accepts online.

falegname.riga: Built-in wardrobes, made-to-measure bookcases, interior doors, stairs, cladding and fitting.
falegname.h1: Joiner's quote: you describe the survey, the draft comes out with your price list
falegname.sottotitolo: Made-to-measure wardrobes, interior doors, stairs and wood cladding. When the survey is done, you tell it the way you would say it in the workshop: the draft takes prices only from your price list and asks you what you haven't said.

esempio.titolo: From the survey to the draft
esempio.intro: A built-in wardrobe, four doors, a staircase to clad and a kitchen to fit, written down with the tape measure still in your pocket. Next to it you see the wardrobe by the square metre of front, the steps counted per piece, the handrail per metre, the client's kitchen as fitting only and the question about the shelves.
esempio.lavoro: Bedroom, hallway and internal staircase, house on two floors
esempio.dettatura: Segno quello che abbiamo visto dalla signora Barbieri. In camera un armadio a muro nella nicchia, più o meno due e quaranta di larghezza per due e sessanta di altezza, ante scorrevoli in rovere e l'interno attrezzato. In corridoio cambio tre porte a battente, laccate bianche, e la quarta la faccio scorrevole a scomparsa, il controtelaio c'è già. La scala di legno la rivesto: sono quattordici gradini, pedata e alzata, e poi il corrimano, una quindicina di metri fra scala e soppalco. Sul soppalco una libreria su misura, tre metri per due e venti. In cucina vuole anche delle mensole in rovere, quante non l'ha ancora deciso. La cucina l'ha comprata lei, io la monto e taglio il top per lavello e fuochi. La tinteggiatura dopo i lavori non la faccio, la fa l'imbianchino.

voci.titolo: Typical items in a joiner's quote
voci.intro: Half the work is done in the workshop and half in the house: that's why a carpenter's lines mix square metres of front, pieces, metres of handrail and fittings. The price by wood and finish is yours and comes from your price list. A wood that isn't in your price list stays unpriced.

righe.voce: Armadio a muro su misura, ante a battente
righe.nota: Counted on the front face, width by height. Write the wood species or finish of the doors: that's where the customer compares.

righe.voce: Armadio a muro su misura, ante scorrevoli
righe.nota: Tracks and runners make the difference: write whether they are exposed or recessed, and what type.
Chests of drawers, shelves, hanging rails, shoe racks: each item separate, so the customer can take things out or add them without redoing everything.
Per square metre of front, with the number of shelves inside the line. If it changes, the bill changes.

righe.voce: Porta interna a battente, fornitura e posa
righe.nota: With frame, architraves and ironmongery. For IVA it counts as an interior fixture (infisso interno): see below.

righe.voce: Porta scorrevole a scomparsa, sola anta
righe.nota: When the subframe (controtelaio) is already built into the wall. If it has to be fitted, that's another line.
Building in the subframe is usually not your job: write who does it.

righe.voce: Posa porta interna fornita dal cliente
righe.nota: Fitting and adjusting only. The material is theirs, and you write that down.

righe.voce: Rivestimento gradino in legno, pedata e alzata
righe.nota: Per step, with the wood species and thickness. Winder steps deserve a separate line.
Per metre, with the wall brackets. Say whether the curves are included.

righe.voce: Rivestimento a parete in doghe di legno
righe.nota: Panelling and tongue-and-groove boards. Say whether the support batten is included.
Supply and fitting, or fitting only if the customer bought the skirting board.

righe.voce: Montaggio cucina componibile fornita dal cliente
righe.nota: Per metre of run. Wall units, tall units and built-in appliances: say so in the line.

righe.voce: Taglio e posa piano di lavoro
righe.nota: With the cut-outs for sink and hob. If the worktop is stone, the cutting usually isn't yours.

righe.voce: Regolazione e riparazione ante e porte
righe.nota: Hinges, runners, locks: work by the hour, when you can't know in advance how long it will take.
The customer tends to assume it's included. Write it down, included or excluded.

prezzare.titolo: How to price a joinery job
prezzare.intro: With made-to-measure work, the price depends on things the customer can't see: the board, the wood, the ironmongery, the hours in the workshop. The quote has to show them, otherwise they compare your wardrobe with one from a furniture shop.

punti.testo: Wardrobes and bookcases are almost always priced on the front surface, width times height. It's better to keep the insides out of that, piece by piece: the customer sees what they're paying for and, if they want to spend less, they take out a chest of drawers instead of asking you for a discount.

The measurements you take on the first day are almost never the ones you cut to, especially if floors and plaster aren't finished. Write that the price is confirmed after the final survey, so an alcove that grows by a few centimetres doesn't turn into an argument.

Solid, veneered, matt or gloss lacquered: for the customer it's always "wood". Put the species and the finish inside the line, and keep separate items in your price list. Then comparing with another quote is fair.

Soft-close hinges, full-extension runners, sliding systems: they change the price and how long the unit lasts. Write which type you use. Handles, if the customer chooses them, go under the exclusions.

Kitchens bought wholesale, doors ordered online: the line becomes fitting only. Write that missing or damaged parts from the supplier aren't yours, because it's the first thing they'll ask you to fix for free.

A board cut for that alcove isn't something you can sell on to anyone else. Write in the quote when you ask for the deposit and when the cutting starts: the customer understands, if they read it beforehand.

documenti.titolo: IVA, rules and contracts to keep in mind
documenti.intro: For a joiner the tax rules aren't the same as a bricklayer's: a door and a wardrobe, in the same job, can follow different routes. These are the things that come up most often.

punti.titolo: Interior doors and beni significativi (significant goods)
punti.testo: Replacing the doors in a home is maintenance, at 10%, but internal doors are infissi interni (internal frames), which DM 29/12/1999 puts among the beni significativi (significant goods): the 10% applies to the door only up to the value of the rest of the work, and the part above that goes at 22%. On the invoice the value of the door must be shown separately (circolare 15/E of 2018). If you make the door yourself, its value includes materials and workshop labour, not fitting labour. If you mark it as a bene significativo in your price list, the draft asks you for that value on each line and uses it to split the IVA.

The reduced rate covers maintenance work on homes, not the sale of finished goods. For wardrobes, bookcases and kitchens, even made to measure, don't take the 10% for granted: ask your accountant which rate to use, and enter it that way in your price list.

With a business client, the fitting alone of doors and frames counts as finishing work on buildings, which goes under inversione contabile (reverse charge). But circolare 14/E of 2015 excludes the fitting of furniture. And if you sell a good with the fitting as an incidental part, it's a supply of goods and the reverse charge doesn't apply. The system currently doesn't calculate the inversione contabile: for fitting alone for a firm, check the total before sending it.

If you sign a contract with a private customer away from your workshop, for example at their home, the customer can normally withdraw. But article 59 of the Codice del consumo (Italian consumer code) rules out withdrawal for goods made to measure or clearly personalised. The exception does not apply if the contract comes from a visit by you that the customer did not ask for (art. 59, comma 1-bis). If your job falls under this, check with an adviser how to word it in the quote.

documenti.avvertenza: These are general pointers to help you write a clearer quote. On your own case the last word belongs to your accountant or legal adviser, also because rules and interpretations change.

straniero.titolo: Made to measure for foreign customers
straniero.testo: Someone furnishing a flat for short lets or a second home wants to understand why a made-to-measure wardrobe costs more than one from the furniture shop, and wants to read it in their own language. The quote can go out in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch, with woods, finishes and hardware translated, the Italian text as the binding one and the withdrawal form in their language. You check it in Italian.

voci.d: I price the wardrobe per square metre and the insides per piece. Can that be done in the same draft?
voci.r: Yes. Each line has its own unit: the front per square metre, chests of drawers and shelves by number. If you say ‘two-forty by two-sixty’, the system redoes the sum in the unit of the item in your price list.

voci.d: In my price list I have different prices for oak, walnut and lacquered. How does it choose?
voci.r: Keep one item for each wood or finish, and say which one in your account. If the system can't find the right item, it doesn't pick one at random: the line stays unpriced, highlighted, and you put the price in yourself.

voci.d: I make the interior doors myself in my workshop. What value do I put for the IVA?
voci.r: The production cost: materials and workshop hours, without fitting and without your mark-up. This is the figure the draft asks you for each door marked as a bene significativo (significant good), and from it the draft splits the amount between 10% and 22%. The reminder to check with your accountant is always there.

voci.d: Does a made-to-measure wardrobe get 10% IVA like the doors?
voci.r: Don't take it for granted: the 10% applies to maintenance work on the home, and a made-to-measure piece of furniture can be treated as a sale of goods. Ask your accountant for the right rate before you send the quote.

voci.d: My price list is handwritten in a notebook from the workshop.
voci.r: That's fine too: you take a photo and the items get read. Before using them, check them one by one and correct any that were misread.

voci.d: I ask for a deposit before cutting the panels. Where do I write that?
voci.r: In the payment terms, in your business details: they appear on every PDF and the customer accepts them together with the quote. Keep them short, with the percentage and the point at which cutting starts.

voci.d: The staircase also has some winder steps. Do I put them together with the others?
voci.r: Better not: a winder step costs more than a straight one. Keep two items in your price list and, when you describe the job, say how many of each there are, so they come out on two separate lines.

meta.titolo: Metalworker quote: railings and gates by voice
meta.descrizione: Metalworker quote from your own account: railings, gates, window grilles and automation, by the metre or by the kilo, with the prices from your price list. Online acceptance.

fabbro.riga: Railings and gates, automation, window grilles, iron staircases and small structures.
fabbro.h1: Locksmith and metalworker quotes: tell us the measurements, the draft comes out with your price list
fabbro.sottotitolo: Railings, gates, window grilles, stairs and steel canopies. After the site visit you tell us the measurements and the work the way you'd say it in the workshop. The draft uses only the prices from your price list, per metre, per kilo or per piece, and flags what's missing.

esempio.titolo: From the workshop to the draft
esempio.intro: A driveway gate to rebuild and motorise, the pedestrian gate, the fencing and a balcony railing. Next to it you can see the gate separated from the automation, the customer's own motor as fitting only, fencing and railing by the metre, and the question about the window grilles that the customers haven't decided yet.
esempio.lavoro: House with a garden: gate, fencing and balcony
esempio.dettatura: Faccio il punto sui signori Mariani. Il cancello carraio scorrevole lo rifaccio nuovo, luce più o meno quattro e venti, alto un metro e sessanta, zincato e verniciato, da motorizzare con due fotocellule e il lampeggiante. Il motore l'ha già comprato lui su internet, io lo monto e lo collego. Il pedonale di fianco, novanta per uno e sessanta, con la serratura elettrica. Sulla recinzione cambio i pannelli, una quindicina di metri. Sul balcone smonto la ringhiera vecchia e ne metto una nuova a bacchette, tre e venti di lunghezza. Al piano terra vogliono le inferriate alle finestre, su quante non l'hanno ancora deciso. Lo scavo per la guida e il cordolo li fa il muratore, non li metto.

voci.titolo: Typical items in a metalworker's quote
voci.intro: Workshop, treatments, fitting and automation: a blacksmith's quote mixes kilos, metres, square metres and pieces, and each thing should sit on its own line. The price is yours and comes from your price list; a one-off job that isn't in your price list stays to be priced.

righe.voce: Cancello carraio scorrevole in ferro zincato e verniciato
righe.nota: Clear opening by height. Say whether the floor track, rack and stops are included.

righe.voce: Cancello carraio a due ante a battente
righe.nota: With hinges and a centre stop. If the pillars aren't yours, put them under exclusions.
With lock and handle. It's better to list the electric lock as a separate line.
Motor, control unit, photocells and flashing lamp. State the make or write “equivalent”.
Fitting and connection only. The automatic gate paperwork stays with you: see below.
Adjustments, tests, plate, declaration and instructions. Keeping it separate shows the customer what they're paying for.
Per linear metre, with the handrail. Say whether it's fixed to the floor or to the side.
Based on the window opening. If it opens and has a lock, it's a different item.
With frame, hinges and lock. Customers often mix it up with the fixed grille.
With the posts. The masonry base usually isn't yours.

righe.voce: Scala in ferro a rampa dritta
righe.nota: With sheet steel treads or ready for timber ones. Write the parapet as a separate line.
Structural steelwork is often priced by weight. Give the customer the measurements too: kilos alone mean nothing to them.
If you send it out, write that the delivery time also depends on the galvanizer.
With the RAL colour written on the line, not just said out loud.
Customers forget about the old ironwork. Say whether transport is included.
Work charged by the hour, with the call-out as a separate line if you charge for it.

prezzare.titolo: How to price a metalworking job
prezzare.intro: A gate or a railing can be priced in three different ways, and two good metalworkers can end up at the same number by opposite routes. What matters is that the customer understands what's in it, and what isn't.

punti.titolo: Per kilo, per metre, per piece
punti.testo: Structural steelwork by weight, railings and fencing per metre, gates per square metre or as a lump sum. You can mix units in the same quote. But if you price per kilo, write the measurements too: the customer thinks in metres, not kilos.

This is the item where customers get lost most. Write whether it's hot-dip or cold galvanizing, whether the paint is powder coating or enamel, and what colour. A railing that's just “painted” is an argument put off for later.
Concrete, hollow brick, external insulation: the fixing changes, and so does the price. If someone else does the masonry, put curbs, footings and digging under exclusions, written out in full.
Keep the gate, the automation and the commissioning separate. If the customer buys the motor, the first line goes away but the third stays: you do the tests and the paperwork anyway.

Decorative railings and gates are made from a drawing. Write that the work starts when the customer approves the drawing: one extra bar per metre, once the piece is finished, comes out of your pocket.
A balcony on the third floor isn't fitted like a fence in a garden. If you need scaffolding, a platform or a truck-mounted crane, write who provides them and whether they're included.

documenti.intro: For a metalworker the delicate point is the automatic gate: there the documents are an obligation, not a courtesy. These are the things that come up most often in work for homes.

punti.titolo: Automatic gate: you are the manufacturer
punti.testo: Whoever motorises a gate becomes its manufacturer under the Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC, even if the motor is another make or the customer bought it. At the end of the job you issue the EC declaration of conformity, fix the plate with the CE marking, hand over the instructions and the maintenance log, and keep the technical file. From 20 January 2027 Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies, replacing the directive.

punti.titolo: The electrical part of the automation
punti.testo: The DM 37/2008 (the Italian decree on installations in buildings), in article 1, comma 2, letter a, includes the systems that automate doors, gates and barriers. To connect them you need the qualification for that letter, even if limited to automations, and at the end of the job you must issue the dichiarazione di conformità (declaration of conformity). If you don't have it, write in the quote who does the connection.

Replacing railings or gates on a home is usually maintenance, at 10%. If the same job also includes windows or doors, which are beni significativi (significant goods), the window grilles and bars are not added to their value: circolare 15/E of 2018 treats them as separate goods, independent of the window and door frames, and their value stays within the value of the work.

With a customer who has a partita IVA (VAT number), what counts is how the contract is set up. If you sell a manufactured item and the fitting is only incidental, it is a sale of goods and the inversione contabile (reverse charge) does not apply (circolare 14/E of 2015). If instead it is a works contract on the building, it may apply. Decide it with your accountant before writing the quote: today the system calculates 10% and 22%, not yet the inversione contabile.

documenti.avvertenza: You'll find these here as a reminder for everyday work, not as advice. The actual case should always be checked with your accountant or a technician, and the rules can change.

straniero.titolo: Holiday homes and customers far away
straniero.testo: Someone with a holiday home who wants to secure it with window grilles and a gate before leaving follows the work from a distance and decides from their phone. The quote can go out in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch, with galvanising, painting and automation explained in their language and the Italian text as the binding one. You check it in Italian, and you see when the customer opens it and when they accept it, even from far away.

voci.d: I price railings per metre and canopies per kilo. Can I keep them together?
voci.r: Yes, each line uses the unit of its price list item. Rough measurements you give by eye are redone in the unit of the item. If an item is priced per kilo and you haven't said the weight, the system doesn't make it up: you get a question.

voci.d: The customer bought the motor. Do I still have to do the documents?
voci.r: Whoever motorises the gate is its manufacturer, so yes. In the quote the motor line becomes fitting only, while commissioning with tests and documents stays as an item of yours: keep it as a fixed item in your price list.

voci.d: A job that isn't in my price list, for example a curved canopy?
voci.r: The line stays to be priced, highlighted. You write the price yourself, and if you want you add it to your price list so it's already there next time.

voci.d: I motorise the gate but I'm not qualified for the electrical part. How do I write that?
voci.r: Say it when you describe the job: «the customer's electrician does the electrical connection». It ends up among the exclusions. The dichiarazione di conformità (declaration of conformity) for the electrical part is issued by whoever does the connection.

voci.d: I send the hot-dip galvanising out. How do I tell the customer about the timing?
voci.r: Write it in the name of the galvanising item, for example «zincatura a caldo presso terzi, tempi dello zincatore» (hot-dip galvanising by a third party, timing set by the galvaniser). If it happens every time, put it in the notice at the bottom of the quote, in your business details.

voci.d: I fit window grilles together with someone else's new windows. Does the IVA change?
voci.r: The grilles are not added to the value of the windows: under circolare 15/E of 2018 they are independent goods, and in your price list they should not be marked as beni significativi (significant goods). They stay within the value of the work, at the rate of the work.

voci.d: The job only starts after the customer approves the drawing. Can I write that?
voci.r: Yes. Put it in the notice at the bottom of the quote, in your business details, so it appears on every PDF and the customer accepts it together with the price. The notes in the draft, on the other hand, stay with you.

meta.titolo: Gardener's quote: lawn, hedges and pruning
meta.descrizione: Gardener's quote from your own account of the job: lawn, hedges, pruning, irrigation, green waste disposal, with the prices from your price list. The customer accepts online.

giardiniere.riga: Lawn, hedges, pruning, new plants, irrigation and green waste disposal.
giardiniere.h1: Gardener's quote: you walk round the garden, you tell it, the draft is ready
giardiniere.sottotitolo: Lawn mowing, hedges, pruning, planting and irrigation systems. When you've finished walking round the garden, you tell it the way you'd tell your crew: the draft uses only the prices from your price list and asks you for the measurements you didn't mention.

esempio.titolo: From the walk round the garden to the draft
esempio.intro: A garden to get ready for spring: lawn, hedge, two olive trees, a dead pine and a new flower bed. Next to it you can see the lawn by the square metre, the hedge by the metre, the trees per tree, the customer's own plants as planting only, and the question about how many plants will go in the flower bed.
esempio.lavoro: Garden of a detached house, spring tidy-up
esempio.dettatura: Giro fatto dal signor Gatti. Il prato è sui trecento metri quadri, va arieggiato e riseminato dove si è diradato. La siepe di lauro lungo la recinzione è una quarantina di metri, alta sui due metri, va potata su tre lati. Ci sono due ulivi da potare e un pino secco da abbattere, la ceppaia la fresiamo. Vicino al portico vuole un'aiuola nuova, più o meno quattro per due: le piante le ha già comprate lui al vivaio, noi prepariamo il terreno e le mettiamo a dimora. Poi l'irrigazione a goccia per l'aiuola, con la centralina; quante piante ci vanno non l'ha ancora deciso. Le ramaglie le portiamo via noi. Il pino del vicino che sporge non lo tocchiamo.

voci.titolo: Typical items in a gardener's quote
voci.intro: Lawn, hedges, trees, flower beds and irrigation: in gardening every job has its own unit, and disposal weighs as much as the work. The price is yours and comes from your price list; an unusual pruning job that isn't in your price list stays to be priced.

righe.voce: Taglio del prato con raccolta dell'erba
righe.nota: Say whether collecting and disposing of the clippings is included or whether the grass stays on site.
With removal of the thatch. The customer often mixes it up with mowing.
Seed and covering included. Say that the grass taking also depends on watering.
With the type of fertiliser on the line: base, maintenance, slow-release.
With preparation of the ground. If the ground needs redoing, that's another line.
By the linear metre, but height and sides to be done change everything: write them on the line.
By height: an olive tree and a fifteen-metre pine are not the same item.
With the height and the method: dropped whole to the ground or taken down in sections.
The customer thinks felling includes it. Say whether it's included or not.
Digging over, topsoil, levelling. Extra topsoil can be counted by the cubic metre.

righe.voce: Fornitura e messa a dimora arbusto
righe.nota: With the species and the pot size on the line.

righe.voce: Messa a dimora piante fornite dal cliente
righe.nota: Labour only. Say that you don't guarantee that plants you didn't supply will take.
By volume of material, or by square metre with the thickness written down.
Drip line and fittings. Trenching for the lines, if needed, should be written separately.
With the number of zones. The electrical connection, if it isn't yours, goes under exclusions.
Clippings and brash by volume. Say whether transport and dumping are included.
With the visits and the tasks included written out in full. Anything else is extra.
With the machine and the operator. Say whether transporting the machine is charged separately.

prezzare.titolo: How to price a gardening job
prezzare.intro: In gardening the same job can take an hour or a whole day, depending on what you can't see from the road. The quote is there to show the customer why.

punti.testo: Lawn by the square metre, hedges by the linear metre, trees per tree. Each has its own way, but the customer must be able to redo the sum: if he changes his mind about a stretch of hedge, he knows straight away how much the price changes.

A tall tree with the house underneath isn't pruned like one in the middle of a lawn. Say whether you work with tree climbing or with a platform, and whether the garden can be reached with machines or has to be done all by hand.
It's the item the customer forgets and the one that costs you most. Count it by volume, or say it's included. If the brash stays with the customer, put it under exclusions: no surprises the next day.
If he bought the plants himself, the line becomes planting only. Say that you don't guarantee they'll take: you didn't choose them, and you don't know how they've been looked after.

For ongoing maintenance, a lump-sum item works best, with the visits and the tasks included written out one by one. Everything that isn't there, heavy pruning or redoing work, goes separately with its own price.
Sowing and transplanting have their own time of year. Say that the dates depend on the weather, so a delay because of rain doesn't look like lateness in the customer's eyes.

documenti.titolo: Qualifications, waste and IVA to keep in mind
documenti.intro: For a gardener the rules aren't those of building work: what counts is the qualification, the treatments and above all where the clippings and prunings end up. These are the things that come up most often.

punti.testo: To work on green spaces for other people, legge 154/2016 (article 12) requires registration in the Registro ufficiale dei produttori (official register of producers) or a certificate of competence, issued after a training course under the accordo Stato-Regioni (State-Regions agreement) of 22 February 2018. Some qualifications in the field exempt you from it.

To buy and use plant protection products for professional use you need the certificate of competence required by D.Lgs. 150/2012, known as the patentino (pesticide licence). It lasts five years and is renewed with a refresher course. If you don't do the treatments, write it under exclusions.

After DL 153/2024, converted by legge 191/2024, waste from private garden maintenance done by professionals counts as municipal waste (rifiuti urbani). It can be taken to the collection centres, but only under the conditions of the comune's regulations. To carry it in your own vehicle you need to be registered with the Albo gestori ambientali (register of waste carriers), category 2-bis, with the EER code 20 02 01.

The 10% rate under legge 488/1999 (Italian law 488/1999) applies to the maintenance of buildings mainly used as homes. Garden care is not work on the building, so it is normally invoiced at the standard rate. If the same job includes building work, such as low walls or paving, ask your accountant how to split it. Careful: the system calculates the IVA with questions designed for work on homes, and if you answer that it is a home it applies 10%. For a garden, check the rate before sending the quote.

punti.titolo: No inversione contabile (reverse charge) on gardens
punti.testo: Even with a business customer, garden maintenance doesn't go under inversione contabile (reverse charge): circolare 14/E of 2015 leaves gardens out of the notion of a building, except when they are an integral part of it, like a roof garden or a terrace.

documenti.avvertenza: Take these as a rough guide, not as professional advice. Rules and interpretations change, and for your own case it's your accountant and the relevant offices who decide.

straniero.titolo: Gardens of people who live abroad
straniero.testo: An owner who only comes in summer wants to find the garden in good order and entrusts the season's maintenance to someone from a distance. The quote can go out in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch, with the visits included in the contract listed in their language and the Italian text as the binding one. You check it in Italian, and the customer accepts it from the link, even from far away.

voci.d: The customer says «the whole garden», but I price lawn per square metre.
voci.r: Give a rough size, for example «about three hundred square metres», and the system uses it in the unit of the item. If you don't give a size, it doesn't make one up: you get a straight question, «how many square metres of lawn?».

voci.d: For hedges the height matters, not just the metres. What do I do?
voci.r: In your price list you keep different items for different heights, and when you describe the job you say how tall the hedge is. If the system can't find a matching item, the line stays to be priced and you put the price in yourself.

voci.d: Do I put green waste disposal on its own line or inside the other items?
voci.r: However you prefer, as long as it's clear. If you want a separate line, keep an item per cubic metre in your price list and give the quantity when you describe the job: «three cubic metres of branches to take away». If you only say «we'll take it away», transport stays included in the work items. If instead it's left with the customer, say so and it ends up among the exclusions.

voci.d: I do maintenance contracts for the whole season. Can I use that?
voci.r: Yes. Put a lump-sum item in your price list with the visits and the work included, and the draft uses it when you mention it. Things outside the contract that you describe go on separate lines, with their prices or to be priced.

voci.d: To fell the tree you need a permit. Do I write that in the quote?
voci.r: If it's needed in your case, say it when you describe the job as an exclusion: «the customer applies for the felling permit». Exclusions go under the items in the PDF and the customer reads them before accepting.

voci.d: What IVA do I put on a garden? Every time I'm unsure.
voci.r: For garden care the rate is usually the standard one, not the 10% for work on homes. But the system calculates the IVA with questions designed for work on homes: if you answer that it is a home, it applies 10%. For a garden, check the rate with your accountant before sending the quote.

voci.d: I also do treatments against pests. Do I put them in the quote?
voci.r: Yes, as a separate item, with the product or the type of treatment in the name of the item. If you don't have the licence and someone else does the treatments, say so when you describe the job: they end up among the exclusions.

meta.titolo: Quote from a voice message: you talk, and the draft is ready
meta.descrizione: Quote from a voice message: describe the site visit by voice or in writing, even in your own language. You get back a draft with your price list and questions about anything missing.

preventivo-da-vocale.riga: You describe the site visit as you would to a colleague: the system lines up the items, measurements, questions and exclusions.
preventivo-da-vocale.h1: Quote from a voice message: you describe it, and the system writes the draft
preventivo-da-vocale.sottotitolo: When the site visit is done, you speak into your phone or write a couple of lines, just as you would to a colleague. The system splits the work into items, redoes the sums on the measurements, takes the prices from your price list and asks you about whatever you didn't say. You check it and approve it.

sezioni.titolo: How you describe the site visit
paragrafi: Open the new quote page on your phone, nothing to install. You have two ways: press the microphone and dictate, or type. When you dictate, your phone's speech recognition turns your voice into text: we only receive the text, never the audio. You can read it over and fix it before preparing the draft.

You can also describe the job in your own language. By voice you can choose from Italian, Romanian, Albanian, Arabic, Ukrainian, Russian, Spanish, French and English, if your phone recognises that language; if it doesn't, it tells you and you write instead. In writing any language is fine, even mixed with Italian. The draft always comes out in Italian, and measurements given in another language count the same as those given in Italian.

An example of how you might describe a job (made up): “Mrs Conti's bathroom, she lives there. I'm taking off the tiles up to two metres and the old shower tray. The bathroom is two metres by one eighty. I'll fit an eighty by eighty shower tray, she's buying the sanitaryware, I'll fit it. She's calling the electrician herself.” You don't need anything more.

sezioni.titolo: What happens after you describe it
paragrafi: In a few seconds you get a draft to check. Inside you find what you said, put in order like a quote, and a mark on everything that doesn't add up.

punti.testo: «I take out the old sink and fit the new one» becomes two lines, removal and fitting. «I'll swap it» said in one word stays one line. «I strip it out and take it away» stays a single line: disposing of what you remove is part of the removal. If you say «six sockets» and then list them room by room, it stays one line for six.

If you give the measurements, the system does the sum, not by eye: «two by one eighty» becomes **3.6 m²**. If the item in your price list is measured another way (per metre, per piece, per m² of door) and the measurements are there, the quantity is recalculated in that unit. Two lines with the same item are added together, and a duplicate is removed.

If you didn't give a quantity, the line stays empty and you get a straight question: «How many m² of tiling?». If you gave a number without a unit, it asks you for the unit. For IVA it needs three answers: whether it's a home, what type of work it is, and who buys the materials. If these can't be worked out from what you said, it asks you.

A job that isn't in your price list, or that the system isn't sure it has recognised, stays to be priced and is highlighted, with the reason written next to it. You can pick the right item from the price list yourself or type the price by hand: until you decide, the price stays empty.

What you exclude («she calls the electrician herself») goes under the exclusions, written out clearly beneath the items of the quote. What you put off for later («we'll look at it afterwards») goes in the notes, which stay with you and don't go on the PDF. If the customer buys the materials, the line becomes fitting or installation only.

sezioni.titolo: How to describe it well: a few practical tips
paragrafi: The system understands site talk, rough measurements and changes of mind. But a few habits will get you a more complete draft and fewer questions to answer.

punti.testo: The customer's name, the address of the job and whether they live there. These three details save you a question about IVA and a field to fill in by hand.
Finish the bathroom, then move on to the kitchen. Jumping back and forth still works, but it's more likely that a measurement ends up attached to the wrong room.

punti.titolo: Give the measurements, not just the totals
punti.testo: «Three twenty by two seventy» is better than «about ten metres». If the measurement is by eye, just say so, «more or less»: it is used and marked as approximate.
«She's already bought the porcelain tiles», «I'm buying the sanitaryware». It changes the line (supply and fitting, or fitting only) and it changes the IVA.

punti.titolo: Say what you don't do as well
punti.testo: The chases the plasterer closes up, the aerial, moving the furniture. If you say it when you describe the job, it goes under the exclusions and the customer reads it before accepting.
«Three sockets in the bedroom, no, four» counts as four. The correction only replaces the thing it contradicts: the other lines you said earlier stay.

sezioni.titolo: Why the system never guesses
paragrafi: The quote carries your name. A wrong number that's too low means a job done at a loss, one that's too high means a lost customer. That's why the rules are strict, and they apply to every line.

**Quantities are never estimated.** If a measurement isn't stated and can't be worked out from what you said, the line stays without a quantity and becomes a question. Even a number given in a different unit from the one in the item isn't converted by eye: it asks.

**Prices are never made up.** A price can only come from an item in your price list. If no item really describes that job, or if the match is uncertain, the line stays to be priced. A similar but fuller item (hot and cold water when you only said cold) is not acceptable.

**When in doubt, one line too many.** If it's not clear whether a correction cancels a job you mentioned earlier, the line stays and the doubt goes in the notes: an extra line you can delete in a second, a lost line you won't see.

**You always see where each line comes from.** Next to each item in the draft you find the words you said yourself, «You said: …», so you can tell straight away whether the chosen item is the right one. You can change it, remove the line or add another.
Until a quantity, a price or an answer on IVA is missing, the quote can't be approved: the system tells you what's missing and on which line. And nothing reaches the customer without your approval.

sezioni.titolo: And after the draft
paragrafi: Once you've checked the draft, you approve it: out comes the PDF with your logo and a link you send to the customer, on WhatsApp too, with the message already written. They open it and accept it from their phone: you'll find how it works in [online acceptance](/funzioni/accettazione-online). If the customer doesn't speak Italian, the quote can go out in [their language](/funzioni/preventivo-in-lingua-del-cliente).
If you want to see how the account changes from one trade to another, have a look at the examples for [electricians](/preventivo-elettricista) and [plumbers](/preventivo-idraulico).

domande.titolo: Questions about the quote from a voice note

voci.d: Do I have to speak in a particular way for it to understand?
voci.r: No. Talk as you would to a colleague, with your own words. It helps if, in your price list, next to the items, you write what you call them out loud: the system searches for those words too.

voci.d: If I correct myself while talking, what stays?
voci.r: The final version of what you corrected stays. If you say “three sockets, no, make that four”, the line is for four. The other jobs you mentioned earlier stay where they are.

voci.d: Can I describe the job in Romanian or Arabic?
voci.r: Yes. By voice it depends on your phone: if it recognises your language, dictate; otherwise, type. In writing, any language is fine, even mixed with Italian. The draft always comes out in Italian.

voci.d: Does the customer see what I said?
voci.r: No. The customer sees the quote: the items, the quantities, the prices and the exclusions. What you said and your site visit notes stay with you.

voci.d: What happens if I mention a job that I don't do?
voci.r: If you say someone else does it, or that you won't touch it, it doesn't become a line: it goes under the exclusions or into the notes. But if you do it and it's not in your price list (“that one's extra”), it becomes a line to be priced.

voci.d: I gave the wrong measurement. Do I have to do it all again?
voci.r: No. In the draft you correct the quantity on that line and the total updates. You don't need to record it again.

meta.titolo: Quote in English or German for your customer
meta.descrizione: Quote in the customer's language: English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch. Two-language PDF where the Italian text is the binding one, and the right of withdrawal translated.

preventivo-in-lingua-del-cliente.riga: English, German, French, Spanish and Dutch, with the Italian text alongside, which is the binding one.
preventivo-in-lingua-del-cliente.h1: The quote in your customer's language, with the Italian text as the binding one
preventivo-in-lingua-del-cliente.sottotitolo: You work in Italian as always. Your foreign customer gets the message, the page and the PDF in English, German, French, Spanish or Dutch, with the Italian text alongside. You see the translation and can correct it before you approve.

sezioni.titolo: Who it's for
paragrafi: Houses bought by foreigners, flats let to people who have only recently started working here, second homes of families living abroad. The customer understands the measurements and the prices, but an item like «rasatura» (skim coat) or «massetto» (screed) means little to them, and a quote they don't understand gets signed late, or not at all.

With PreventivoLampo the quote can go out in five languages besides Italian: **English, German, French, Spanish and Dutch**. You choose the language quote by quote. For a customer who speaks yet another language, the quote stays in Italian.

Don't confuse it with the language you use to describe the site visit: that can also be Romanian, Albanian or Arabic, and the draft still comes out in Italian. We explain it on the page about the [quote from a voice note](/funzioni/preventivo-da-vocale).

sezioni.titolo: How it works, and how you check it
paragrafi: The quote starts out in Italian, from what you tell it and from your price list. When you've sorted out the items, quantities and prices, you choose the customer's language in the draft and press the button to translate. Each translated item appears under the Italian one, and you can correct it by hand, line by line. The same goes for the exclusions.

punti.testo: Item names and exclusions go through the translation. Numbers, quantities, prices and rates aren't touched: they come from the quote data. Measurements and formats (80x80, Ø 16), abbreviations and brand names stay exactly the same.

punti.titolo: Trade words have a fixed translation
punti.testo: Massetto (screed), tramezzo (partition wall), battiscopa (skirting board), rasatura (skim coat), idropittura (water-based paint), punto luce (light point), a corpo (lump sum), fornitura e posa (supply and fitting), solo posa (fitting only): for terms whose meaning changes if they're badly translated, the translation is fixed in advance, language by language. A tramezzo stays a non-load-bearing dividing wall in German too.

punti.titolo: If you change an item, the translation is redone
punti.testo: If after translating you edit, add or remove an item, the system notices and asks you to redo the translation. Until it's up to date, the quote can't be approved: the customer always reads the same things you approved.

punti.titolo: You see what they will see
punti.testo: After approval you can open the page exactly as the customer sees it, in their language, and the two-language PDF.

sezioni.titolo: The PDF in two languages
paragrafi: The PDF stays an Italian quote, with the Italian always up front. Under each item there's the translation, in grey italics. The column headings, the taxable amount, IVA, the total, the exclusions and the conditions each have their line in the customer's language. Dates are written the way they read them.

IVA stays the Italian one, and the PDF explains to the customer which rate applies and why. If there are «beni significativi» (significant goods, a category with its own IVA rules), the term stays in Italian, with an explanation in their language: it's a word from Italian law, and translating it would make it vaguer.

At the bottom there is the prevailing-language clause, written in both languages: the quote is drawn up in Italian and in the customer's language, and if the two differ, the Italian text prevails. The Codice del Consumo (Italian Consumer Code) requires that information for consumers be given at least in Italian (art. 9), and in distance contracts the customer can ask for it in Italian (art. 49, paragraph 7): the translated version is a help for them, the one that counts is the Italian one.

sezioni.titolo: The message, the acceptance page and the withdrawal in their language
paragrafi: When you send the quote on WhatsApp, the message is already written in the customer's language, with the quote number, the total and the link.

The page they open is in their language: the total, the breakdown of items, the exclusions, the button to accept and the sentence they tick before doing it. Under each translated item there's the Italian one, and at the top they can switch to the Italian version with one tap. You'll find how acceptance works in [online acceptance](/funzioni/accettazione-online).

The information on the right of withdrawal and the standard form are in their language too, on the page and in the PDF, where the withdrawal page comes in Italian and in the customer's language. These texts aren't our own translation: for each language they start from the official version of the form set out in Directive 2011/83/EU, which exists in all the languages of the Union. What changes, and what doesn't, when the customer is foreign is covered in the guide to the [quote for foreign customers](/guide/preventivo-cliente-straniero).

sezioni.titolo: What stays in Italian, and why
paragrafi: Some things stay in Italian on purpose. It's worth knowing before you send the quote.

punti.titolo: The Italian text of the quote
punti.testo: It's always there, above the translation, and it's the binding one. It's also the one you check.

punti.titolo: The payment terms and the notice you write yourself
punti.testo: The payment terms and any notice at the bottom of the quote are written by you in your business details, and they aren't translated. Keep them short and clear, with figures as numbers: a deposit as a percentage is understood in any language.
The draft, your account of the site visit, the notes and your price list stay in Italian. The customer doesn't see them.
The customer's name, the address of the job and your business details are written as they are.

domande.titolo: Questions about the quote in another language

voci.d: Do I need to know English to send a quote in English?
voci.r: No. You prepare it and check it in Italian. The system does the translation, and if a translated item doesn't convince you, you correct it or get help from someone who knows the language, before you approve.

voci.d: The customer speaks Portuguese. Can I send it in their language?
voci.r: Not for now: the customer languages are English, German, French, Spanish and Dutch. In other cases the quote goes out in Italian, or in English if the customer reads it.

voci.d: If there's a dispute, which text counts?
voci.r: The Italian one. The clause is written in the PDF in both languages, and the sentence the customer ticks to accept repeats it.

voci.d: Does the customer see the Italian too?
voci.r: Yes. In the PDF the Italian comes before the translation, on the page each translated line has the Italian one underneath it, and with one tap the customer can switch to the all-Italian version.

voci.d: I translated the quote and then changed a quantity. Do I have to translate it again?
voci.r: No: quantities and prices are not translated, so the translation is still valid. You only need to redo it if you change the text of a line or of an exclusion, or if you add or remove one. The system tells you.

voci.d: Does the price change if the quote is in another language?
voci.r: No. Prices, IVA (Italian VAT) and total are the same as in the Italian quote: only the language the customer reads them in changes.

meta.titolo: Quote accepted online, with name and time
meta.descrizione: Online acceptance of the quote: the customer opens the link, reads the PDF and accepts with their first and last name. You keep the date, the time and a copy of the accepted PDF.

accettazione-online.riga: The customer accepts from the link, with no sign-up. You see when they open it and when they reply.
accettazione-online.h1: Online acceptance: the customer says yes from the link, and you keep the proof
accettazione-online.sottotitolo: You approve the quote, send the link, the customer opens it on their phone and accepts it with their first and last name. You see when they opened it and when they replied, and you keep the name, date, time and the PDF they accepted.

sezioni.titolo: From your OK to the customer's link
paragrafi: When the draft is right, you approve it by ticking that you have checked prices and quantities. At that moment the PDF with your logo and the customer's link are created. From then on the quote can't be edited or deleted: the customer must be able to accept exactly what you approved. If something changes, you prepare a new quote.

To send it you have two buttons. **Send on WhatsApp** opens the chat with the message already written: greeting, quote number, total including IVA (Italian VAT) and link. **Copy the link** is for email, SMS or any other channel.

sezioni.titolo: What the customer sees
paragrafi: The customer opens a page that belongs to your business, not to us: at the top your name with your partita IVA (VAT number), and your logo if you've uploaded it. They don't need to sign up or install anything, and the page opens on a phone just as on a computer.

punti.testo: At the top they read the total including IVA, with the taxable amount and the IVA shown separately and the date until which the quote is valid. Below, the main jobs and the detail of all the lines, with quantity and price.

punti.titolo: The exclusions and the full PDF
punti.testo: What is not included is written in plain words before the accept button. The full PDF downloads with one tap.
The information on the right of withdrawal (recesso) and the standard form are on the page, to open if the customer needs them.

To accept, they type their first and last name, tick ‘I have read the quote and I accept it on the terms stated’ and press the button. They can also reply that they don't accept: you see that too, with their name.

sezioni.titolo: Sent, seen, accepted: you always know where it stands
paragrafi: In the list of your quotes each one has its status: to check, sent, accepted or rejected. Inside the quote you see three steps with date and time: approved by you, seen by the customer, customer's reply.

‘Seen’ is marked the first time the customer really opens the page. The preview WhatsApp shows under the link doesn't count: there the customer has only seen the title, not the quote. To see whether they've opened it, reload the quote page.

The quote is valid for the number of days you set in your business details. After the expiry date the customer can still read it, but can no longer accept it from the link: if they want to go ahead, you send them a new quote, maybe with updated prices.

sezioni.titolo: What you keep
paragrafi: When the customer replies, the quote's log keeps the name they typed, the date and time, the IP address they replied from and the fingerprint of the PDF they had in front of them: a code that identifies that exact document. The PDF you reopen from your area has a box at the bottom saying «Accettato online da» (accepted online by), the name, the date and the time.

Let's be clear: **it is not a digital signature**, and not a qualified electronic signature either. The page tells the customer this too, before they accept. It is an acceptance with name, date and time on a document that can no longer change, and it is far more than what you have today with a message.

sezioni.titolo: The withdrawal form
paragrafi: If the customer is a consumer and accepts at a distance, from the link, or after a visit made at their home, as a rule they can withdraw without giving any reason. The period is 14 days: for labour only it starts from acceptance, but if the quote also includes materials you supply, it starts from the day the customer receives them. It becomes 30 days if the contract comes from a visit of yours that the customer had not asked for. The information on withdrawal and the standard form are already ready: on the customer's page and on the last page of the PDF, with your contact details and the quote number. If the customer is foreign, they will also find them in [their own language](/funzioni/preventivo-in-lingua-del-cliente).

If the customer wants you to start before the period has passed, get them to ask for it in writing, on paper or by email, together with an acknowledgement that once the work is finished they can no longer withdraw. The acceptance page does not collect this request. With the request, if they withdraw after you have started they pay you for the part of the work already done; without it, they owe you nothing. What it is best to do in practice is explained in the guide on [withdrawal from a quote accepted at home](/guide/recesso-preventivo-accettato-a-casa).

sezioni.titolo: Why it's better than an ‘OK’ on WhatsApp
paragrafi: An ‘OK, go ahead’ in a chat doesn't say which version of the quote it refers to, whether the customer read the exclusions, or whether the total they have in mind is the same as yours. At the end of the job, when they ask why painting the ceiling isn't included, all you have is their word and a screenshot.

With the link the customer accepts one specific document, which doesn't change after approval, and does so after seeing the total, the lines and the exclusions. You keep the name, date, time and the PDF. And it's easier for them than a signature on paper: they read the quote and accept it from their phone, with no appointments and nothing to print.

voci.d: Is it a digital signature?
voci.r: No, and we don't tell the customer it is either: the page says it is not a qualified electronic signature. It is an online acceptance with name, date, time and the accepted PDF, which you keep as proof.

voci.d: Does the customer have to download an app or create an account?
voci.r: No. They open the link on their phone or computer, read and reply. All they need is their first and last name.

voci.d: Can I change a quote I've already sent?
voci.r: No: after approval the document is locked, because the customer has to accept exactly that one. If something changes, you prepare a new one and send the new link.

voci.d: How long does the customer have to accept?
voci.r: You choose the number of days of validity in your business details, and the customer sees the expiry date on the page and on the PDF. After that, the link no longer takes replies.

voci.d: Do I get an alert when the customer accepts?
voci.r: Not a notification: you see the reply in the list of quotes and inside the quote, with name, date and time. To find out whether they've opened it in the meantime, reload the page.

voci.d: What if the customer doesn't want to accept online?
voci.r: The PDF can be downloaded and printed like any other quote, and you can have them sign it on paper. Acceptance from the link stays there, if they change their mind.

meta.titolo: Your price list, from Excel or from a photo
meta.descrizione: The price list is the basis of every quote: you upload it from Excel, PDF or a photo and check it line by line. Prices come only from there, never made up.

listino-prezzi.riga: Excel, PDF or a photo of the handwritten sheet: the prices in your quotes come only from there.
listino-prezzi.h1: The price list: quotes use your prices, and nobody else's
listino-prezzi.sottotitolo: You upload the price list you already have, even handwritten, and check it before using it. From then on every price in the draft comes from one of your lines. Anything that's missing is left to be priced, and if you want it goes into the price list for next time.

sezioni.titolo: Prices come only from your price list
paragrafi: When you [describe a site visit](/funzioni/preventivo-da-vocale), the system looks up each job among the items in your price list and picks only from those. If an item really describes the work you mentioned, the line takes its price and unit. If no item fits, or the match is uncertain, the line stays **to be priced**: no market prices, no averages, no estimates.

No price list, no start: you make your first quote once you have at least a few items. If you change a price in the draft, the change applies to that quote only and is recorded as your own price. The price list never changes by itself.

sezioni.titolo: How to upload it, and how to check it
paragrafi: The price list you already have is fine. Nothing goes into the price list until you've checked and confirmed it.

punti.testo: Upload the .xlsx or .csv file as it is. Columns are recognised by their headings (Descrizione, U.M., Prezzo: description, unit, price). If the headings aren't clear, the system tries to work them out, and you can pick the columns by hand and have the file read again. An old Excel file (.xls) must first be saved as .xlsx.

punti.titolo: From PDF, photos or old quotes
punti.testo: You can upload a PDF, several photos together of a handwritten sheet, or a few old quotes. The system transcribes the price items and skips headings, totals, IVA and terms. From old quotes it takes the unit price, and if an item appears several times with different prices, it flags it. It doesn't transcribe customers' names.

Before importing, you see all the lines. Those with a doubt (a unit you can't read, a hard-to-read price) are in yellow, with the reason: correct them or untick them. Units written in lots of different ways (mq, ml, nr, pz, a corpo) become the ones used in the quote. Missing or repeated codes are assigned by the system, and the ones already in your price list are not overwritten.

punti.titolo: If you don't have a price list
punti.testo: You can type in the jobs you do most often by hand, one at a time. Or you can start from a sample price list with prices taken from public price lists: until you change them, they stay marked as sample prices, and we remind you to check them before you send real quotes.

sezioni.titolo: Trade words: what you call items out loud
paragrafi: In the price list an item is called «Rasatura pareti con stucco», but on site you say 'skim it', 'fill the lot', 'a coat of skim'. That's why every item has a field, **what you call it out loud**: a few words, separated by commas. When the system looks for the right item, those words count for more than the name and the description.

After an import the field is empty. It's worth filling it in for the items you use most, with the words you really use, site slang included. A few minutes is enough, and later drafts find more items first time. Every item can also have a longer description, which helps the system understand what it includes. The quote shows the item's name, which you can always tweak in the draft.

sezioni.titolo: When an item is missing, and how the price list grows
paragrafi: A line to be priced is highlighted in the draft. You can pick an item from the price list yourself, or type the price by hand. If you type the price, you can tick 'suggest adding it to my price list at this price'.

When you approve the quote, the ticked lines go to the **To price** page. There you decide at your own pace: you add them to the price list with name, unit and code, or you press 'Not needed'. A suggestion never goes into the price list by itself. The ones you add come back next time with their price, without you typing it.

There's another typical case: the customer buys the materials. If an item in your price list includes the material (you mark that on the item), then with the customer's material the line becomes labour only and stays to be priced, because the supply-and-fit price would be wrong. If your price list also has a labour-only item for that job, the draft can use that directly; otherwise you set the price.
If you delete an item from the price list, quotes already made don't change. Same if you change its price: a quote already prepared keeps the prices it had.

sezioni.titolo: The beni significativi (significant goods)
paragrafi: In home maintenance IVA is 10%, but some goods only partly qualify. These are the beni significativi (significant goods) of the DM 29/12/1999: lifts and hoists, external and internal doors and windows, boilers, video entry phones, air-conditioning and air-recirculation equipment, bathroom sanitaryware and taps, security systems.
